Case File No DRT-ED-NOBODY · Special File · Nobody Behind the Wheel
Last Year, a Tesla Drove Itself From the Factory to a Customer’s Home. This Year, Its Driverless Miles Grew Eightfold in One Quarter.
In June 2025, Tesla delivered its first car with no one inside, straight from its Austin factory to a buyer’s door. This week, it reported nearly 2 million unsupervised robotaxi miles and a car with no steering wheel already carrying passengers. Each step that once sounded impossible is becoming routine.
Threat level 3/5 — Guarded
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
The first time you see a car pull up with nobody in it, it doesn’t feel real. Then you see it again, and again, and it starts to feel normal. That’s how technology changes the world: slowly, then all at once. Self-driving cars may be entering the “all at once” phase.
The evidence board
| | The Milestones
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the first delivery.** In June 2025, a new Tesla drove itself from the company’s Austin factory to a customer’s home with no one in the car.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the miles.** Tesla said on October 21 that cumulative unsupervised robotaxi miles grew eightfold in the third quarter to nearly 2 million.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the vehicle.** The Cybercab, built without a steering wheel or pedals, began giving rides in Austin on September 3.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit D — the reach.** Tesla’s supervised self-driving software has 1.74 million active subscriptions and is now approved in nine EU countries.
| OUR THEORY
---
Every driverless car depends on hardware and software that let it see the road and make decisions in a split second. Those pieces are bought for every vehicle. That’s why the suppliers behind them can grow even faster than the car companies themselves.
Connected file
| | Musk’s Next Target
---|---
Musk’s companies are moving into phones too. SpaceX agreed in 2025 to buy wireless spectrum from EchoStar for $17 billion and filed a “Starlink Mobile” trademark. Musk has publicly denied building a phone, but said a Starlink device is “not out of the question at some point.”
One analyst believes all the evidence points the same way.

The crowd was fired up from the moment doors opened, the energy was high, and President Obama was as inspiring as ever.

He also reminded us about the stakes in this race, and he couldn’t be more right. Senate control is on the line, and the GOP is backing Jon Husted with an almost unlimited amount of money.

The polls are neck and neck, so these next 10 days until Election Day matter _a lot._

We are falling short of our $1 million goal, so I’m going to you directly: **I need you and 93 other people reading this email to chip in $5 before midnight tonight, or else we might not have the resources we need to win this race.**

clean_body: | | | Today’s rally with President Obama was absolutely incredible. The crowd was fired up from the moment doors opened, the energy was high, and President Obama was as inspiring as ever. He also reminded us about the stakes in this race, and he couldn’t be more right. Senate control is on the line, and the GOP is backing Jon Husted with an almost unlimited amount of money. The polls are neck and neck, so these next 10 days until Election Day matter a lot. We are falling short of our $1 million goal, so I’m going to you directly: I need you and 93 other people reading this email to chip in $5 before midnight tonight, or else we might not have the resources we need to win this race. Will you chip in $5 now to help us hit our goal and flip this seat? We’ll be tracking donations here: = Thank you. Sherrod | This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. # New Ad Drops; Wes Moore Scrambles.
******ALERT***** WE NEED TO RAISE THE FINAL $40,000 FOR THE CLOSING TV ADS THIS WEEKEND. [](https://us.list-manage.com/VRseXWYZZTs?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) Dear friend,
We just dropped a new Ad "Meet Dan" and I hope you [watch it](https://us.list-manage.com/jGt9ixvK0QE?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) here or click the video link below. We hope you like it - this campaign is to renew our State for the sake of everyone's future. If our seniors and retirees have to continue to move out of state because of the rising taxes, costs and fees, then our children will not have a future here either.

But we are closing in on the win, friend. Wes Moore is running so afraid, he scrambled to bus people to the polls just to cheer him on while he voted, and he's rushing back to Maryland from being out of state (again!) in order to campaign in Prince George's, Montgomery County and...**get this...Hagerstown, Maryland tomorrow!** **He's desperate because he knows the wind is at our backs and we will win**.

**But to do so, we need your help with our final TV ad purchase**. In order to distribute this TV Ad to our Cable and Streaming Buy on Monday, we need to finish raising the [$40,000 needed funds](https://us.list-manage.com/12oI0quAzKe?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) and we have a budget need to double that to finish out expenses. This is not a typical fundraising appeal - it is a truly time sensitive need I am sharing with you.

If everyone reading this e-mail were able to donate $300 tonight we would raise the necessary funds.

So I have contributed another $20,000 to the campaign effort as just filed in our reports. Now, I'm asking you to match that tonight. I need your help - now, not later.

It only takes [$176](https://us.list-manage.com/11Q2vlYWD8E?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) for one TV ad spot. Would you chip in [$300](https://us.list-manage.com/8CkKETQdlOf?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b)? Or could you help us urgently at 10 spots ([$1776](https://us.list-manage.com/NQnBRyfpu12?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b))? Let's win together. Thank you.

For Maryland,

Dan Cox
Candidate for Governor of Maryland

**I. The party that invented modern politics -- and died of silence**
In 1840, the Whig Party invented modern American campaigning. Log cabins, hard cider, barrels of cheap whiskey rolled to the polls, "Tippecanoe and Tyler Too" sung in every county seat. They put William Henry Harrison in the White House, counted Henry Clay and Daniel Webster among their orators, and for two decades they were the governing conscience of the Republic -- banks, tariffs, roads, canals, the American System.
Twelve years after their greatest triumph, they were gone. Not defeated in battle. Evaporated. In 1852 they nominated a genuine national hero, General Winfield Scott, and lost in a landslide. By 1856 they were a footnote in the very states they had once carried.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/16ede31f-0b0e-4588-8923-11d50bd4a6fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Whigs did not die of a rival's brilliance. They died of silence. For a generation, the one question that grew louder every year -- the extension of slavery into the territories -- was the question the Whigs refused to answer. Their conventions passed "silence" planks. Their leaders sought "truce." They believed, as every dying party has believed, that voters would keep showing up for the coalition instead of the cause...

[ https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/28?c0=deluzio-em-26-q4.4eyHU-&refcode=em261025&refcode2=153.42639.2AfoIY&t=1030&akid=153%2E42639%2E2AfoIY ]'Pittsburgh Post Gazette: State, federal lawmakers rally in support of
Allegheny County paid parental leave policy -- Allegheny County Executive
Sara Innamorato was joined by Democratic state and federal officials
Thursday in issuing a call for the county health board to pass
Innamorato’s proposed paid parental leave policy next week. The county
health board is scheduled to vote on the proposal — which would provide 12
weeks of paid parental leave for eligible county residents — on Monday. If
passed, the measure will go before County Council next month. Innamorato,
who is due to give birth to her first child this fall, was joined by
lawmakers including U.S. Reps. Chris Deluzio and Summer Lee, state Reps.
La’Tasha Mayes and Aerion Abney, and state Sen. Nick Pisciottano, at a
press conference at the Western Pennsylvania Diaper Bank in Point Breeze.
“These are elected representatives who don’t just talk about being
pro-family, but are actually willing to step up, to spend political
capital, and to take the action necessary to get pro-family policies
across the finish line,” Innamorato said. Monday’s vote will follow months
of debate on the issue. The policy that goes before the health board has
been revised since the original proposal that would have provided 18 weeks
of paid parental leave. Brought for public comment in May, the initial
plan received mixed reactions from hundreds of county residents who
submitted comments to local officials. In response, the Board of Health
announced sweeping changes to the policy earlier this month, reducing the
length of paid leave to 12 weeks and implementing a small-business cap
that would exempt businesses with fewer than 15 employees. “The county
listened to feedback on the paid parental leave policy and we made several
adjustments,” Innamorato said. More than a dozen states have enacted
mandatory paid parental leave policies, while another nine have adopted
voluntary paid parental leave systems that allow the benefit in the
private insurance market. Pennsylvania has no statewide parental leave
policy, although Sen. Pisciottano, D-Allegheny, introduced legislation in
March that would provide 12 weeks of paid leave to employees who have
worked their jobs for at least a year. That bill was referred to committee
upon introduction but has yet to receive a committee vote or hearing.
Meanwhile, the state House passed a paid family and medical leave bill in
March. That legislation has since stalled in the Republican-controlled
Senate. In June, the Pennsylvania Senate Labor and Industry Committee
voted 9-2 in a bipartisan move to pass the Family Care Act, which would
establish a paid family and medical leave program for up to 20 weeks for
eligible workers for the birth of a child or a serious personal medical
issue. Sponsor Devlin Robinson, R-Allegheny, said the act would fund the
program through employee payroll contributions and be administered by the
state Department of Labor and Industry. The legislation has yet to go to
the Senate floor for a vote. A federal paid parental leave policy — the
FAMILY Act — was introduced in September 2025 and would create a national
paid family and medical leave insurance program. The bill — co-sponsored
by U.S. Reps. Deluzio and Lee, among others — was referred to committee
upon its introduction, but has not advanced to a House floor vote. “Let’s
be honest, this is an issue that should be handled at a federal level,”
Lee said. “We shouldn’t have to be here, county by county, municipality by
municipality, or state by state, ensuring our families are taken care of.”
In lieu of that legislation, Deluzio applauded Innamorato and her
administration for pursuing a paid parental leave policy locally. “When
you go through something as important as starting a family, having a baby,
you shouldn’t be risking your job or your safety to care for yourself and
your baby,” he said. Deluzio said that he supported the recent changes to
the Allegheny County proposed policy made, in part, in response to input
from small business owners. “They were smart,” he said. “They reflected
feedback from the community and small business owners, especially.” State
Rep. La’Tasha Mayes, co-chair of the Black Maternal Health Caucus, said
most mothers, about 60%, return to work within three months of giving
birth — many within six to eight weeks. “You bring a baby into the world
and then you must return to work,” she said. “Your life has changed. Your
mind has changed. Your body has changed. Your thoughts should be about how
you heal and how you take care of your new baby, but the competing
thoughts are, ‘I’ve got to get back to work.’” Mayes said the policy would
ultimately help prevent maternal deaths, particularly for Black women who
have a significantly higher rate of maternal mortality than the national
average, and two and a half times higher than their white counterparts,
according to the county health department. Nationally, the CDC found that
the U.S. maternal mortality rate was 17.9 deaths per 100,000 live births
in 2024. '

# [](https://act.electjon.com/go/4629?t=1&akid=3180%2E5691347%2EIbZXSd)

Let me guess, Peter: when you open up your email inbox, you’re bombarded with emails from political campaigns or advocacy organizations, some of which you’ve never heard of.
I know it’s a lot.
And it’s why in a sea of promises that “Donald Trump is FINISHED” and breathless “5X MATCH NOW!!!” emails, I work really hard to make sure our messages are different.
No scammy tactics. No fake matches. Only real, honest updates about my work in the Senate and this reelection campaign in Georgia.
But here’s the truth: The vast majority of donations we receive come from supporters just like you, who opened this email and decided to give a lot or a little to this campaign. It all adds up, and I couldn’t be more grateful to every single one of you.
So yes, this is another email asking for money. I wish I didn’t have to keep asking, but winning a Senate race in battleground Georgia takes a massive amount of resources. [**I hope you’ll join me by making your first donation today.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-oct26.FRbHBd&refcode=em261025-1-subs&utm_campaign=em261025-1-subs&t=2&akid=3180%2E5691347%2EIbZXSd)
Here’s a link: [**https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ossoff-em-oct26**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-oct26.FRbHBd&refcode=em261025-1-subs&utm_campaign=em261025-1-subs&t=3&akid=3180%2E5691347%2EIbZXSd)
The Trump administration is out of control. They have lied us into war. They've sent prices skyrocketing.
They're abusing federal power. Every single day, the President and the First Family are lining their own pockets, to the tune of billions of dollars.
It has never been more important in American history that we restore checks and balances, because if we're not able to constrain and contain and slow down this attack on our Constitution, I don't know that we have free and fair elections in 2028.
And winning the Senate majority is essential to containing the catastrophic damage this administration is doing.
We have to defend this crucial Senate seat in Georgia. I am the only Democratic Senator up for reelection in a state that Donald Trump won. I can win again, but only with your help.
[**So please: Take a moment to donate $5 — or whatever makes sense to you today — to my reelection campaign. We’ll put your donation straight to work getting out the vote like never before and decisively winning this Senate race.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-oct26.FRbHBd&refcode=em261025-1-subs&utm_campaign=em261025-1-subs&amount=5&t=4&akid=3180%2E5691347%2EIbZXSd)

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Let’s finish what we started
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
The work is paying off, but we have to keep fighting

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3063%2E4032634%2Enqu7ZM)
---
There’s a feeling you get on election night that’s hard to describe unless you’ve been through it. You’re watching the numbers come in, refreshing the results, holding your breath. You think about all the people who knocked on doors, made phone calls, and gave up their evenings and weekends because they believed we could win. You feel the energy of the moment — and you feel hope. As I travel across the country, I’m seeing crowds that are electrified by the opportunity to make their voices heard. Candidates are making their case in diners, union halls, and school gyms. Volunteers are knocking on doors and making calls. People are ready to make their voices heard and send a message to Donald Trump and the Republicans. Because here’s the thing: working people know Republicans want to rip health care away from millions of families so billionaires can get even bigger tax breaks. They’re watching Republicans go after Social Security, gut public education, and slash cancer research. They know Republicans are putting Donald Trump ahead of the people they were elected to represent. And they’re really and truly ready for something different. I’m sure you are too. Now, I’ve been in enough elections to know that being right isn’t enough. Having better ideas isn’t enough. Even having the polls on your side isn’t enough. You have to win the votes. We cannot underestimate what Republicans will do to hold on to power. We’ve watched them bend the rules, ignore the Constitution, and stand by while Trump puts his own interests ahead of the American people. They won’t give up their power without a fight. So we have to keep fighting, too. All the way to the finish line. With a Democratic Congress, we could finally hold this administration accountable with public hearings, real oversight, and tough questions under oath. We could stop rubber-stamping policies that benefit the wealthy at everyone else’s expense and get back to lowering costs, protecting health care, and fighting for working families. **And honestly, I don’t just want us to win. I want us to win BIG.** Big enough that nobody can dismiss the results. Big enough to send a clear message that this country is ready to go in a different direction. That kind of victory doesn't happen by accident. It happens because people refuse to sit it out. They show up, organize, and bring others along. I’ve seen what this grassroots team can do. I know what happens when people who care about their country decide to do something about it. It’s not always glamorous. It’s not always easy. Sometimes it feels like progress is moving a whole lot slower than it should. But no matter what, one thing will always be true: This work matters. We know what we’re fighting for. We know what’s at stake. And we know how to win. Thanks for being part of this, Elizabeth | **Elizabeth Warren is fighting corruption, holding Trump accountable, and making government work for working families. Chip in now to help elect Democrats who will fight back this November.** | [**DONATE NOW**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3881?t=8&akid=3063%2E4032634%2Enqu7ZM)

clean_body: The work is paying off, but we have to keep fighting | | | There’s a feeling you get on election night that’s hard to describe unless you’ve been through it. You’re watching the numbers come in, refreshing the results, holding your breath. You think about all the people who knocked on doors, made phone calls, and gave up their evenings and weekends because they believed we could win. You feel the energy of the moment — and you feel hope. As I travel across the country, I’m seeing crowds that are electrified by the opportunity to make their voices heard. Candidates are making their case in diners, union halls, and school gyms. Volunteers are knocking on doors and making calls. People are ready to make their voices heard and send a message to Donald Trump and the Republicans. Because here’s the thing: working people know Republicans want to rip health care away from millions of families so billionaires can get even bigger tax breaks. They’re watching Republicans go after Social Security, gut public education, and slash cancer research. They know Republicans are putting Donald Trump ahead of the people they were elected to represent. And they’re really and truly ready for something different. I’m sure you are too. Now, I’ve been in enough elections to know that being right isn’t enough. Having better ideas isn’t enough. Even having the polls on your side isn’t enough. You have to win the votes. We cannot underestimate what Republicans will do to hold on to power. We’ve watched them bend the rules, ignore the Constitution, and stand by while Trump puts his own interests ahead of the American people. They won’t give up their power without a fight. So we have to keep fighting, too. All the way to the finish line. With a Democratic Congress, we could finally hold this administration accountable with public hearings, real oversight, and tough questions under oath. We could stop rubber-stamping policies that benefit the wealthy at everyone else’s expense and get back to lowering costs, protecting health care, and fighting for working families. And honestly, I don’t just want us to win. I want us to win BIG. Big enough that nobody can dismiss the results. Big enough to send a clear message that this country is ready to go in a different direction. That kind of victory doesn't happen by accident. It happens because people refuse to sit it out. They show up, organize, and bring others along. I’ve seen what this grassroots team can do. I know what happens when people who care about their country decide to do something about it. It’s not always glamorous. It’s not always easy. Sometimes it feels like progress is moving a whole lot slower than it should. But no matter what, one thing will always be true: This work matters. We know what we’re fighting for. We know what’s at stake. And we know how to win. [ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
Derek, there’s a
phrase in this business I’ve never liked: Going dark.

It means our ads stop running. Not because we wanted them to, but because
the money ran out.

Here’s what that actually looks like: A voter in Pittsburgh turns on the
local news next week and sees a dozen ads about this race. If we go dark,
every single one of them was paid for by my opponent’s Mar-a-Lago donors.

Every attack unanswered. Every lie unchallenged. Every undecided voter
hearing exactly one side (even when it’s lies).

Here’s the problem: These next nine days are the most expensive days of
the entire cycle. Ad time in Pennsylvania right now costs a multiple of
what it cost in September, and the far-right has a mountain of cash we’ll
need to respond to.

But what we have instead are grassroots supporters like you giving what
they can, when they can.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/20450?amount=25&t=1001&akid=771%2E245147%2EgLcEVB ]So yes, we have ads reserved through November 3rd — but reserved isn’t
paid for. And with only nine days left, there’s no more time to make up
this gap later if we fall short. Please,
Derek: Will you rush
$25 or
whatever you can right now to keep our ads on the air through Election
Day? Here in Pennsylvania, the last thing a voter hears about a candidate
is usually the thing they remember in the booth.

They’ve seen the polls tightening. They’ve seen the election forecasters upgrading our chances. They’ve seen everyone from Nate Silver to Fox News to The New York Times to The Cook Political Report saying what six months ago seemed impossible: We can really flip this Kansas Senate seat.

We increase our ad buys, up our canvassing and phone banking efforts and make sure Kansans far and wide know that there is a different way forward than the chaos and corruption we’re currently seeing from Washington. But all that takes a _lot_ of resources.

What if we said the overwhelming amount of donations GIFFORDS receives aren’t massive checks, or pallets of cash flown in on private jets?
#

Friend, we've got a simple question to ask you:
Is there anything — ANYTHING at all — we can say to convince you to make a donation to GIFFORDS PAC ahead of the election to help us counter the hundreds of millions of dollars Elon Musk is pouring in during these final weeks?
What if we told you that GIFFORDS has committed $10 million through November, putting us in the top five single-issue organizations spending in this election?
What if we said the overwhelming amount of donations GIFFORDS receives aren’t massive checks, or pallets of cash flown in on private jets?
And what if we told you the vast majority of those donations come through emails like this, from people like you, who care about gun violence and know that electing a Democratic Congress is how we’ll put an end to it?
We don’t have endless budgets. We don’t have an army of billionaires powering this work. What we do in these next two weeks depends almost entirely on the support of supporters like you, and we’re humbly asking for your help.
**[Can you please make a donation of $3 or anything you can to GIFFORDS PAC to help us cover the cost of our final push? We need a ton of donations to keep pace with our goals, and we can’t fall short.](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q42026.PjNIJI&refcode=em261025-1-b&t=1&akid=11964%2E3935704%2E0QtzcV)**

name: Sherrod
subject: Worried, but not for the reasons you might think
body:
Thank you for having my back, again and again.
|
#
| | | | | Hi Peter – Roy Cooper here. My friend Sherrod Brown is running for U.S. Senate over in Ohio, and he needs our support. If you can, [**_I hope you'll split a donation between our grassroots campaigns.**_](https://act.roycooper.com/go/19285?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1718&amount=5&t=7&akid=4858%2E124072%2ELJWs6e)

If you'd no longer like to receive these partner emails, [**_you can opt out here._**](https://act.roycooper.com/signup/unsub-tandems/?t=8&akid=4858%2E124072%2ELJWs6e)
---|---
Peter:
We're just under two weeks out from Election Day, and the pressure is on. But not for the reasons you might think...
The truth is: **I don’t want to let you down.**
_You_ are the heart of this campaign. Since the very beginning, grassroots donors have made it possible to compete with massive spending from special interests. You’ve proven that when working people come together, we can win:
* When Peter Thiel dropped $3.6 million against me in a single week, you helped keep our own ads live.
* When JD Vance personally attacked me, you stood by me and helped this campaign surge ahead.
* And when crypto billionaires decided to put $30 million behind new attack ads spreading lies about me, you helped us fight back.

But this race is far from over, Peter.
All eyes are on Ohio, and the money continues to _pour_ in. **In fact, Republican megadonors are spending more here than in Georgia, Alaska, and North Carolina combined. Let that sink in.**
I’m not sharing this to scare you – the polls keep proving that we have what it takes to win – but I’m writing this to remind you just how important you are to this movement.
**In the face of a quarter of a BILLION dollars being spent by Republicans in Ohio, our campaign has been able to stay competitive _only_ because of grassroots donations from folks like you. And right now, I need you to have my back more than ever.**
My past races have taught me that this close to Election Day, resources are what allow a candidate to pull ahead. So we cannot give the GOP an inch.
[**_Today, I’m asking you to split $5 between my campaign and Roy Cooper. I’m counting on you. Will you give what you can to help us flip Ohio and take back the Senate?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/19285?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1718&amount=5&t=9&akid=4858%2E124072%2ELJWs6e)
Thank you for keeping us in this fight,
Sherrod Brown
| |
* * *
[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1718&t=1&akid=4858%2E124072%2ELJWs6e)
Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

**_[Donate today to help win this seat and flip the Senate blue.](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1718&source=&t=2&akid=4858%2E124072%2ELJWs6e)_**

name: Tim Walz
subject: A real opportunity in Kansas
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Small Town PAC, [smalltownpac
body:
Cindy is a state senator, former substitute teacher, and proven leader who has spent years fighting for working families.
#
Peter,
I'm proud to endorse Cindy Holscher for governor of Kansas.
Cindy is a state senator, former substitute teacher, and proven leader who has spent years fighting for working families. And with just 10 days until Election Day, we have a real opportunity to help her win.
[**Will you split a donation between Cindy's campaign and Small Town PAC today to help her reach voters, fight back against Republican attacks, and finish strong?**](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-partner-cs-2026102.ZMHk4U&amount=5&refcode=em20261025-1255&t=1&akid=1255%2E34582%2EgA_EZf)
Cindy grew up on a farm, the daughter of a veteran and union construction worker and an elementary school employee. Thanks to her father's good union job and strong public schools, her parents were able to give her opportunities they hadn't had themselves.
That's the kind of opportunity every family deserves. And it's exactly what Cindy is fighting to protect.
When she saw Kansas politicians putting wealthy special interests ahead of working families, Cindy decided to do something about it. She ran for office, won, and has spent years fighting for the people and communities she represents.
Now, she's running for governor to lower costs, strengthen public schools, expand access to affordable health care, and make sure rural communities aren't left behind.
**Here's the deal: Cindy has a proven record of service and knows what it takes to earn people's trust. And with just 10 days left, this is our chance to help her take that experience to the governor's office.**
[**Will you join me in supporting Cindy by splitting $5 or whatever works for you between her campaign and Small Town PAC? Let's help her win this race and give Kansas families the governor they deserve.**](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-partner-cs-2026102.ZMHk4U&amount=5&refcode=em20261025-1255&t=2&akid=1255%2E34582%2EgA_EZf)

With gratitude,
Tim

name: Abdul El-Sayed
subject: We’re toast
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Tammy Baldwin for Senate
body:
Peter,
If you’ve been keeping an eye on the fight to retake a Democratic majority in the Senate, you probably already know that competitive seats in states like Maine, Texas, and Alaska are currently in play for Democrats. That is massively exciting news.
But as much as I want Democrats to win those races, we have to be realistic about the math. The fact of the matter is that **Republicans only need to flip Michigan in order to hold onto their majority.**
If they flip this seat in Michigan, our chances at winning the Senate are _toast._
I don’t say all this to scare you, but I want to be honest about what this means for our race:
* Republicans have made me their **#1 target to beat** in November, and they are dropping $1 million a day on ads from now until Election Day.

* That means the hundreds of thousands of Michiganders who are currently choosing whether to vote for me, Mike Rogers, or whether to even vote at all are being **swamped with attack ads** in this final push.

We have already defied the odds once and fought this race to a virtual tie. Now, we have to finish the job. The window to make a difference in the outcome of this race is closing fast, so if you’ve been waiting for the right moment to make a contribution to our campaign, _this is it._ **[Will you please donate $5 to my campaign and Tammy Baldwin so we can hold onto this must-win Senate seat? The path to a Democratic Senate runs straight through Michigan.](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/6050?c0=em-ms-tb-20261025-elsayed.Beu8F9&amount=5&refcode=em20261025-5769&t=1&akid=5769%2E35263%2ENN0SuI)**

Thank you,
Abdul

body:

---
| | | | | | | |
Friend,

Here in Pennsylvania, we know exactly how

body:
[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/54940?refcode=em20261025-61931&t=1001&akid=61931%2E1407376%2EbRpDEk ]Demand Justice PAC[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/54940?refcode=em20261025-61931&t=1002&akid=61931%2E1407376%2EbRpDEk ]Demand Justice PAC

Ten federal
judges. One result: more power for corporations and the ultra-wealthy,
less for everyone else.

Together, they’re enabling the slide toward Oligarchy. Take a look:

#1: Judge Andrew Oldham: called our entire system of administrative law
“constitutionally suspect,” a view that threatens the EPA, OSHA, and the
CFPB.

#2: Chief Judge Reed O’Connor: ruled the entire Affordable Care Act
unconstitutional, a theory so extreme the Supreme Court reversed it 7-2.

#3: Chief Judge Amos Mazzant: struck down overtime pay for 4 million
workers and blocked a law targeting anonymous shell companies.

#4: Judge James C. Ho: reported 26 reimbursed trips, including a Cancun
junket paid for by the right-wing group behind overturning Roe v. Wade.

#5: Judge Don R. Willett: wants to revive the legal doctrine courts once
used to strike down minimum wage and child labor laws.

#6: Judge Edith H. Jones: argued for a theory that would have destroyed
the CFPB, the agency that has returned over $21 billion to consumers.

#7: Judge Victor Marrero: approved the T-Mobile/Sprint merger despite
objections from 14 state attorneys general. The combined company shed
roughly 14,000 jobs.

#8: Judge J. Campbell Barker: helped kill a rule that would have raised
franchise and contract workers’ pay by $1.06 billion a year.

#9: Judge Ada E. Brown: nullified the FTC’s non-compete ban, costing 30
million workers more than $400 billion in wages.

#10: Judge Sean D. Jordan: wiped out overtime protections for another 4
million workers, then killed a rule keeping medical debt off credit
reports.

Workers, consumers, and patients lose. Corporations and billionaires get
richer. Several of these judges have their lifestyles bankrolled by the
same conservative legal network shaping the bench, and we’re calling it
what it is: corruption.

Demand Justice PAC is fighting back: naming names, exposing the money and
influence behind these rulings, and fighting to restore independence to
our courts.

$5 today to help us fight the judges enabling the slide
toward Oligarchy?

Ken

Here is how it works. The ballot now comes with two envelopes: one to seal the ballot in, and a second to put that envelope in.

_Do you recognize this kid?_
Growing up in Manchester, Chris Pappas attended the city's public schools, knew his neighbors by name, and learned early what it means to be part of a community.
As a teenager he worked at his family's restaurant scooping ice cream and eventually helped run the landmark business, serving generations of Granite Staters. When you're part of a business like that, it's hard to see where the business stops and the community starts. They're one and the same, and Chris has carried that spirit with him ever since.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dcabf1a8-d58f-46ee-b2c8-4564d6b93b82?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Chris now lives with his husband Vann in the same area he grew up in.
After graduating college he ran for the state legislature to give back to the city that had given him so much, and his neighbors sent him to Concord. A decade later he stepped up to run for and win a seat on the Executive Council.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dcabf1a8-d58f-46ee-b2c8-4564d6b93b82?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Years later, when he ran for Congress, people said a Democrat couldn't hold that district for more than one term. Granite Staters elected him four times in a row in one of the swingiest districts in the country.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dcabf1a8-d58f-46ee-b2c8-4564d6b93b82?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In Washington Chris has been an independent-minded Democrat, rated one of the most bipartisan members of the House and willing to work with anyone to help New Hampshire's families.
Now he's running for Senate. People doubted Chris before, and grassroots supporters proved them wrong. With just 9 days left in this race, we need to do it one more time.
**[Will you chip in $25 now to boost our grassroots campaign and send Chris to the Senate this November?](https://substack.com/redirect/dcabf1a8-d58f-46ee-b2c8-4564d6b93b82?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/dcabf1a8-d58f-46ee-b2c8-4564d6b93b82?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
For Chris this race is personal. He understands the struggles Granite Staters are facing, and he's ready to go to Washington to fight special interests, protect reproductive freedom, lower costs, take on the big companies pricing people out of their own communities, and build a fairer, freer New Hampshire for everyone.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dcabf1a8-d58f-46ee-b2c8-4564d6b93b82?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
We are building a strong grassroots team that's ready to win on November 3rd. Volunteers are knocking doors across the state, and grassroots supporters are stepping up every single day.
But Trump's allies are flooding the airwaves with millions to stop Chris. We can't let them outwork us in the final stretch. We need the resources to compete, reach voters in every corner of the state, and make sure Granite Staters hear directly from Chris about what he'll fight for in the Senate.
**[Rush $25 or whatever you can to keep our momentum going, defend New Hampshire's open seat, and flip the Senate blue.](https://substack.com/redirect/dcabf1a8-d58f-46ee-b2c8-4564d6b93b82?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

New Hampshire means everything to Chris. He's grounded in the Granite State. He knows what matters because he's lived it, and he'll carry the stories of Granite Staters with him to the Senate.

clean_body: A message from Team Pappas | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more A message from Team Pappas | | | Oct 25 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Do you recognize this kid? Growing up in Manchester, Chris Pappas attended the city's public schools, knew his neighbors by name, and learned early what it means to be part of a community. As a teenager he worked at his family's restaurant scooping ice cream and eventually helped run the landmark business, serving generations of Granite Staters. When you're part of a business like that, it's hard to see where the business stops and the community starts. They're one and the same, and Chris has carried that spirit with him ever since. | | ---|---|--- Chris now lives with his husband Vann in the same area he grew up in. After graduating college he ran for the state legislature to give back to the city that had given him so much, and his neighbors sent him to Concord. A decade later he stepped up to run for and win a seat on the Executive Council. | | ---|---|--- Years later, when he ran for Congress, people said a Democrat couldn't hold that district for more than one term. Granite Staters elected him four times in a row in one of the swingiest districts in the country. | | ---|---|--- In Washington Chris has been an independent-minded Democrat, rated one of the most bipartisan members of the House and willing to work with anyone to help New Hampshire's families. Now he's running for Senate. People doubted Chris before, and grassroots supporters proved them wrong. With just 9 days left in this race, we need to do it one more time. For Chris this race is personal. He understands the struggles Granite Staters are facing, and he's ready to go to Washington to fight special interests, protect reproductive freedom, lower costs, take on the big companies pricing people out of their own communities, and build a fairer, freer New Hampshire for everyone. | | ---|---|--- We are building a strong grassroots team that's ready to win on November 3rd. Volunteers are knocking doors across the state, and grassroots supporters are stepping up every single day. But Trump's allies are flooding the airwaves with millions to stop Chris. We can't let them outwork us in the final stretch. We need the resources to compete, reach voters in every corner of the state, and make sure Granite Staters hear directly from Chris about what he'll fight for in the Senate. New Hampshire means everything to Chris. He's grounded in the Granite State. He knows what matters because he's lived it, and he'll carry the stories of Granite Staters with him to the Senate. Thanks for being part of this campaign. -- Team Pappas | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Chris Pappas PO Box 313, Manchester, NH 03105 ? ?

You've heard Democrats talk about a "blue wave" this year. But what's really powering their Senate campaigns is a GREEN WAVE of cash. And it's crashing over the Senate map right now. Look at the latest FEC reports, covering July through September: ▶ **TEXAS** : James Talarico (D) raised $60.2 million. Ken Paxton (R) raised $10.2 million.
▶ **KANSAS** : Adam Hamilton (D) raised $9.4 million. Roger Marshall (R) raised $800,000.
▶ **GEORGIA** : Jon Ossoff (D) raised $33.1 million. Mike Collins (R) raised $2.8 million.
▶ **FLORIDA** : Angie Nixon (D) raised $7.2 million. Ashley Moody (R) raised $2.1 million.
---
[](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=267efbc9f90c4cc885b840030ef5b51e&_e=yU8lX0py4iljY3A94rNtpg9W_IASQQ9qM0Niwl2wcSicc1WIue54FchIR5TLB_XJ5fAZDEqI2WOX8ucwbL23pXZ3DmFmYFK-t3JnuRE5tKVmzlULnB93OHSrVrgS3XCR2lugbaFWM82yUhMhXoSH15d5_GNjD5ZRQi7MB5OV3PYVbwgoBuQmP3PyLR2k2OcfozL3HbjnZYqvM6rUPEykxRHza17oLoyOs4KljCMuq-hVR2Yx8Ya0knGUSGmWyqfNmWAX-NLqEwmfltE4f277vIEecIv9T9xk6gqEF6ZNMG-ogbjxuOpk46T3EhSMWElxaYJou-HnqMsYOF0AZj63adt7i91toZ3vCYsJbr9ALtv3s9wTlmj_UmvWCbdjfN9k2OCzhzd-eaAH2oGCtpTkZg%3D%3D)
---
You may have seen headlines bragging about record Republican super PAC money. The GOP's top Senate super PAC just raised a record $272.9 million in a single quarter. Here's what those headlines leave out: **a super PAC dollar doesn't go nearly as far as a candidate dollar.** Federal law requires TV and radio stations to sell ad time to candidates at their LOWEST UNIT RATE in the final 60 days before a general election. That's the same rate the station gives its best commercial customer. Super PACs don't get that rate. They pay whatever the station charges. During a football game in Austin in September, a Republican super PAC was charged $450,000 to air a single ad. Talarico's campaign paid $50,000 for a spot in the same game, in the same market. **That's NINE TIMES the price.**

---
**So when Democrats send money straight to their candidates, every dollar buys MORE airtime than a super PAC dollar.** And that's exactly what they're doing. For years, the Left has built a national small-dollar machine. Liberal donors don't just give to candidates at home. They give to candidates in states they've never visited. Talarico has raised more than $122 million from individual donors this cycle, and more than $65 million of it came from small donors giving $200 or less. If James Talarico wins in Texas, it will be because of that mountain of small-dollar contributions. **[We need to use the same national model to fight back: direct contributions to our candidates.](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=267efbc9f90c4cc885b840030ef5b51e&_e=yU8lX0py4iljY3A94rNtpg9W_IASQQ9qM0Niwl2wcSicc1WIue54FchIR5TLB_XJ5fAZDEqI2WOX8ucwbL23pXZ3DmFmYFK-t3JnuRE5tKWwhFMxP9uH7uRLtjrtmw1ELKep7Q-vlByB-G5epESBlQHUiXW5E7nm7GigSvxE0HQmORKMD5qfdYt8wM0qvSV2GcmoZqmvPCOq1xSAStH_VM_z1KyFHQys8tWobCaJGEHBLduyJNZ3eoH9fRtIuJmnv2bIwhN7eLIFCy9lXtwDTSc7uZhOkNcb0lHb7ZxYdcqjkt5mzd14v7ijgy0-8gUVL2HwbeyTehtZcaR-bKzUyImyg32A9FMcPidOnTnuype4SrZ9yskLqoN5F1s17abUqUxBj69HmFwrPc3zFusdVw%3D%3D)** Once your money moves away from the candidate's own campaign, it buys less. | Peter,
Trump's allies are already talking about how they could hold on to the House even if Democrats win it back in November.
A right-wing think tank founded by the architect of Project 2025 just published a memo laying out how Congress could refuse to seat elected representatives. It even spells out the steps they want Republicans to take, all the way to declaring someone's seat vacant and forcing another election.
And who do they single out? Proud Democratic Socialists like me, along with our Muslim friends and other groups they claim are a "threat" to the Constitution.
Here's what they wrote:
---
| [](https://irrem7hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001yaAx7W-M6WKTJQm44PnN7wv8UttGtrb5suNJZVX0vsOgeJwpNIfs5z_SABLXGDUY3UQD9d8zMugsJaGpbVqvVxmdfbs4r00Nu9-CjVqcnZWYZECoxW7CPbVwnNiSI4iioL_goE-kyrylNEhikSNZbOJSqiMfpbemTRrjn3VKmjGy5UOzlU1-ouX9s6GUgmcIQPrnj2LafuFGMX7q5b0lEMAp803Jui0KfffhfxgvQkYZWguJFOdUfkZVG8SLWVAu&c=e_R_U4YgZ0vTXBbva4iwr5DfpZ3K64kwhhCR2gwDLayDRUCSz8FE3Q==&ch=ikhLHncUcYz8R_gJoPaWMXveK8GZfXbZl5cN4hU29ae6hySKul9xaQ==)
---
Their argument is that Congress could investigate whether someone can truly swear loyalty to the Constitution, then use that "judgment" to overturn an election.
I find it pretty rich that people who want to question someone else's loyalty to the Constitution are proposing ways to violate it.
Peter, my intention is never to fearmonger, but after everything we've witnessed over the last few years, we have every reason to take this seriously.
Trump tried to overturn the 2020 election, his allies pushed a fake electors scheme, and a mob stormed the Capitol on January 6. Mike Johnson, who helped challenge the election results, is now Speaker of the House.
Now, just days before the election, a group closely tied to Trump's administration is laying out how Congress could deny voters the representatives they choose, as if a seat in Congress belongs to whoever holds power in Washington instead of the people who cast the votes.
I don't know whether Republicans will try to use this plan in January. But the memo is real, the proposed steps are there in black and white, and we've already seen how far Trump was willing to go after losing one election.
[We're ready to defend the votes cast in our district and the right of every community to choose its own representatives. name: Darline Graham
subject: Our South Carolina race by numbers.
body:
We have 9 days left. Let me explain what's at stake. |
---

Fellow Patriot -

Here's a breakdown of our race ... _by the numbers_.

**$9 million:**
This is how much Annie Andrews raised last quarter.
I got into this race long after she was already raising millions of dollars from liberals all over the country. She has the support of Hollywood stars like Star Wars' Mark Hamill and Roseanne's John Goodman.

**Whatever happened to the Emergency Broadcast System?** The Emergency Broadcast System was introduced in August 1963, built so the president could reach every radio and television set in the country within minutes of a nuclear attack. It was tested every week for decades. If you were there, you remember the ambush. Mid-cartoon, mid-ballgame, mid-movie, the picture would cut away to a slide carrying your local station's call letters and those three words, and then [two blended tones, 853 and 960 hertz](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2O6jAQxfGncTqiydj5cOHiSogKbreitAZnQrwyNkqGRLz9in2Fbc-RfsX_evEXiinm-396sJOp-Mz7mliEF5-ntHJ4LVHeoeTAS15zvM8iHgG7QwMHbD0FiRv7phrdxIysK3ZNb9GiQcBqdt3IFgE0wQSgezJ9q4eArR6N6YZAVXQfrgFsG0Db2toMgWi49cS2o8E2ygCPUcpSf5eYZeYpvcvGSx3Ko0puFnmuSv9TeFJ42ve9fpeXvG78-T8LSZiVPm1KH_fxeb5ezl6OX9XixuceU4pr1ysD9wfF9EvK30JsDn8CAAD__xTUciA), would grind away for 20 to 30 seconds. No warning, no pattern you could predict, no appeal. Those tones are still legally fenced off today: in 2015, the FCC upheld $1.4 million in fines against Viacom and ESPN for slipping them into a movie trailer for the film [_Olympus Has Fallen_](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2upDAQhE8DmUd2D38OHGxC9jbdEHlMG3pl2iO7H2huv2Kv8LKSSvWpqv58LV-eEvH22x_oJOaF8aoJRbAsHFPF8F1IPiFzwMKVadtFFtAwKKMV9IsPQicupl1dRAR8tujMaMFCBxra3aEJfW9wmrohjqN5GR1NjMPT2gmhD31L7sYZDb3RYHv76Kbg_fQaPdrBT9Y0ncaVJJfH30wsO8b0ySeWR8hHm9wu8q7N81cDcwPzdV2P8Kr3jNtvYL5lA_NJPuRDYX2zisS4KqM6dVBKlFnFXFT5ZibelF-rukh2hQeWDTl8lE9YRElmvFFtcev7upN1GJtOb4en9L-N_OzD08G_AAAA__-o3IiB). It was never activated for a national emergency, and neither has its successor been, in all the years since--except for that one Saturday that the real emergency code was sent by accident. On Feb. 20, 1971, at 9:33 a.m., a civilian teletype operator at Cheyenne Mountain reached for the weekly test tape and grabbed the wrong one. The message clattering out to some 5,000 radio and 800 television stations carried the day's genuine authentication word--HATEFULNESS--and ordered every station in America to drop its programming. Six botched cancellations later, the correct code word, IMPISH, went out at 10:13. Forty minutes. Only about one station in five followed the rules; plenty assumed an alert arriving at the usual test time had to be a mistake. It was. Nobody was disciplined. Ultimately, the EBS gave way to the Emergency Alert System on January 1, 1997, doing the same job, with a harsher squawk, and now a buzz in your pocketed cell phone, too. It still earns its keep locally: tornadoes, Amber Alerts, flash floods. It's not ancient history, either: In a few weeks, on Nov. 17, FEMA will run another nationwide test at 2:20 p.m. Eastern. Sixty-three years on, the script hasn't meaningfully changed. But remember: _This is only a test._ _Do you remember the Emergency Broadcast System alerts? Cholesterol and blood pressure numbers can look great while the real problem, the one no standard checkup looks at, keeps getting worse inside the heart itself. | Whatever happened to the Emergency Broadcast System? The Emergency Broadcast System was introduced in August 1963, built so the president could reach every radio and television set in the country within minutes of a nuclear attack. It was tested every week for decades. If you were there, you remember the ambush. Mid-cartoon, mid-ballgame, mid-movie, the picture would cut away to a slide carrying your local station's call letters and those three words, and then , would grind away for 20 to 30 seconds. No warning, no pattern you could predict, no appeal. Those tones are still legally fenced off today: in 2015, the FCC upheld $1.4 million in fines against Viacom and ESPN for slipping them into a movie trailer for the film . It was never activated for a national emergency, and neither has its successor been, in all the years since--except for that one Saturday that the real emergency code was sent by accident. On Feb. 20, 1971, at 9:33 a.m., a civilian teletype operator at Cheyenne Mountain reached for the weekly test tape and grabbed the wrong one. The message clattering out to some 5,000 radio and 800 television stations carried the day's genuine authentication word--HATEFULNESS--and ordered every station in America to drop its programming. Six botched cancellations later, the correct code word, IMPISH, went out at 10:13. Forty minutes. Only about one station in five followed the rules; plenty assumed an alert arriving at the usual test time had to be a mistake. It was. Nobody was disciplined. Ultimately, the EBS gave way to the Emergency Alert System on January 1, 1997, doing the same job, with a harsher squawk, and now a buzz in your pocketed cell phone, too. It still earns its keep locally: tornadoes, Amber Alerts, flash floods. It's not ancient history, either: In a few weeks, on Nov. 17, FEMA will run another nationwide test at 2:20 p.m. Eastern. Sixty-three years on, the script hasn't meaningfully changed. But remember: This is only a test. Do you remember the Emergency Broadcast System alerts? Here is what I need from you before November. | | | | Friend, I have studied American elections for sixty years. I have won them and lost them. I have watched majorities built and watched them collapse. And I want to tell you something about this moment that I do not think is being said clearly enough: If Republicans hold the Senate and build on the Trump agenda, we establish a durable governing majority that the left will spend years trying to dismantle. If we lose — if Schumer takes that gavel — we hand the radical left a platform and a megaphone at the exact moment their most extreme candidates are winning primaries in states we should never have to defend. I have seen this movie before. I know how it ends when conservatives stay organized. I also know how it ends when they don't. Friend, before November I need to know where you stand on the issues that will define this election. Not as a poll. As a record. | I made my prediction earlier this cycle. I stand by it. name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: It’s time to lower the Medicare eligibility age
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
Right now, people in their late 50s and early 60s are paying some of the highest premiums of anyone on the private market.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20261025-6879-footer&t=1&akid=6879%2E420207%2EADp_i5)
Peter,
**I just introduced a bill to lower the Medicare eligibility age to 50 from 65.**
Right now, people in their late 50s and early 60s are paying some of the highest premiums of anyone on the private market. They’re old enough to need more care, but too young to get Medicare. That gap is costing people their savings, their health, and sometimes their lives.
My bill closes it.
Across party lines, Medicare is one of the most popular programs this country has ever created. Because it works.
That’s why it’s critical that we start expanding Medicare to more people. **My north star is still passing Medicare For All** , and this bill is a great way to get the ball rolling. Because every time we expand Medicare to more people, we prove that it works.
But Big Pharma and the for-profit insurance industry will fight this with everything they’ve got, because everyone who moves onto Medicare is a customer they can’t squeeze for profit anymore.
I don’t take a dime from corporate PACs, so I can’t match their lobbying budgets. But what I do have is a people-powered movement, and I need it behind this bill from day one.
[**Will you chip in $3 or whatever you can today to help grow our movement and build the pressure we need to make this bill — and Medicare For All — a reality?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261025-1.bxYLA-&refcode=em20261025-6879&amount=3&t=2&akid=6879%2E420207%2EADp_i5)

Healthcare is a human right. Let’s win it together.
In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal

## Homicides Falling in San Antonio
San Antonio is on track to finish the year with fewer than 100 homicides for the first time since 2015. Police Chief Jesse Salame told the city's Public Safety Committee that SAPD [recorded 66 homicide cases](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2upSAUhZ8GOwzsq4gFxTR0d9opzRa2RzIIBjh65u0nzitMt5KVrJ_v1_fyjSGG9PqJB5n22fKS6K6RWqOynBFTJiypngVDJbcTlUjoFxCguBQcxgVdCxctA3berMLPsiMjpxlmUHIcut1MSkyTlsMMSs0wghd6IqnVqhUpvcoumCdOChilFPAF_Sq1d3qV47SOG26aDYJ8aLn0badGH6xb_JMvKr3LRxfN3tpZ2dcPBpaBve-7_12xPSYD-_xhYGN2GBnYp4qBleLRAwNbMXFMLaeQucvv6PmOF_F38lS4FILv-QgueKp8y4VvodTGWziI15AccRByZGC7Yvx5hxhDVRMbxOvAEP_ta__L9TLwNwAA__-r2orX) from January through September. A note from Senator Ashley Moody |
---
Friend,
I'm going to be honest with you, because I don't know any other way to say this.
My heart breaks for France right now. City halls burning to the ground. More than 600 police officers injured in a single day. Rioters tearing the French flag off the monument to their own Republic – and raising a Palestinian flag in its place, while others march under the hammer and sickle.

# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261025_1_buttigieg.hA1J5v&refcode=em20261025-2522&t=1&akid=2522%2E299639%2EHgpeAd)
Hi Peter, it’s Pete Buttigieg.
I know you’re busy, so I will give you the bottom line up front: I’m reaching out today because I am proud to support Gina Hinojosa for Governor of Texas, I believe she will win, and [**I hope you’ll join me in supporting her by making a contribution to her campaign.**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261025_1_buttigieg.hA1J5v&refcode=em20261025-2522&t=2&akid=2522%2E299639%2EHgpeAd)
Before I tell you more about why I know Gina can win in November, I want to share a story about how on-the-ground campaigning, combined with the right candidate, made history in Texas before.
In 1990, Ann Richards was down by double digits in the final months of her race for governor – before she went on to shock the political world with her victory. Now, all signs point to a similar shockwave this November.
Fast-forward to this past March, where Democrats turned out in record-breaking numbers for the primary.
In the months since, Gina Hinojosa has closed a 10-point gap against Greg Abbott and now holds a 4-point lead in the polls. That's the kind of movement you see right before a race breaks our way.
I think part of why Gina is breaking through is that she's not asking Texans to pick a side in some left-versus-right fight. She's asking a simpler question: is this right, or is this wrong? Is it right that the cost of living keeps climbing while the people at the very top get another tax break? Most Texans already know the answer, no matter who they've voted for in the past.
Gina has the momentum. Gina has voters ready to turn out for her. What she needs now, in these final 9 days, is the resources to reach every one of them – to get her message into every part of the state before Election Day, and to answer the attacks that are coming her way.
**[So, I am asking you personally: Will you make a donation to Gina Hinojosa's campaign today and help her make history this November?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261025_1_buttigieg.hA1J5v&refcode=em20261025-2522&t=3&akid=2522%2E299639%2EHgpeAd)**

Thank you,
Pete Buttigieg

Charlie said it best in the days leading up to President Trump's victory in 2024: _" I don't care about polls. __ __I don 't care about betting markets. __ __I don 't care about vibes. __ _ **_I care about how many ballots are in the box. _**_ __If we turnout, we win. __ _**_Do the work. body:
[ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
Derek — here’s
something most people don’t know about how a campaign spends its last
week.

Across Pennsylvania, there are thousands of mail-in ballots that haven’t
been sent back yet. Sitting on kitchen tables, in stacks of mail, in the
glovebox. Every one of them belongs to someone who intended to vote.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/20426?amount=25&t=1001&akid=769%2E245147%2Eh1veIW ]Getting those ballots filled out and returned before 8PM on Election
Day is one of the most important things we can do. But how many of those
intended votes we can turn into actual votes comes down to the resources —
the texts, calls, and people at doors with reminders. So
Derek, can you chip in
$25 to
help keep that operation running at full speed through next Tuesday?

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/20426?t=1002&akid=769%2E245147%2Eh1veIW ]Rush a Donation →

Here’s the catch,
Derek:

There’s a second group we’re racing to reach too, and it’s Pennsylvanians
who haven’t requested a ballot at all. For them, the clock runs out at 5PM
this Tuesday, October 27th. After that, it’s in-person voting or nothing.

A voter who meant to participate and didn’t is the quietest way to lose in
the most competitive state in the nation, where outcomes have been decided
by make-or-break margins.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/20426?t=1003&akid=769%2E245147%2Eh1veIW ]So please,
Derek: Donate any amount you
can today. Because those ballots sitting on thousands of kitchen tables

Early Vote Action

Patriot, Let me explain why I'm so fired up about ballot chasing -- because the math is beautiful. Every Republican vote we "bank" early frees campaigns to stop chasing that voter and focus everything on turning out the people who haven't voted yet. Bank 20,000 votes early, and the path to victory gets dramatically easier. And study after study shows there's nothing more effective than a knock on the door. A note from Senator Ashley Moody |
---
Friend,
I'm going to be honest with you, because I don't know any other way to say this.
My heart breaks for France right now. City halls burning to the ground. More than 600 police officers injured in a single day. Rioters tearing the French flag off the monument to their own Republic – and raising a Palestinian flag in its place, while others march under the hammer and sickle.
Communists and radical Islamists, side by side in the streets. **That 's not a coincidence. That's an alliance.** And it has eyes on more than Europe.
This radical movement is working to infiltrate our own country – and it's counting on patriots like you not realizing it until it's too late.
It is the honor of my life to serve as Florida's U.S. Senator. My state is full of people who already know how this story ends. Families who fled Castro with nothing but the clothes on their backs. Venezuelans who watched their country get looted by socialists in a single generation. Nicaraguans who escaped Ortega. They came here because America was the one place it couldn't happen.
Here, that movement has a fellow traveler on the ballot, and her name is **Angie Nixon.**
She runs a bookstore called "Cafe Resistance." On its wall hang portraits of convicted cop killers – including Assata Shakur, who murdered a New Jersey state trooper and fled to Castro's Cuba. When she was confronted about it, she said she stands by "everything in this bookstore."
She closes her speeches with a line from the Communist Manifesto – "We have nothing to lose but our chains" – and she took that chant to a CAIR gala. She was one of just 7 votes against teaching students the history of communism. She signed the pledge to abolish ICE. She voted against tougher penalties for people who assault police officers.
And she just raised $7 million to take Florida's U.S. Senate seat – more than we raised in the same three months. And Bernie Sanders just pointed his $23 million war chest at this race and came to Florida himself to campaign for her and turn out the vote.
This is a special election – the biggest Senate race in the country this year – and some new polls say it's within the margin of error. If she wins, she becomes **the first dues-paying member of the Democratic Socialists of America in the U.S. Senate.**

My husband is a police officer. I spent my career as a prosecutor, a judge and an attorney general. I've stood with the families of officers who were attacked. I've stood in rooms full of people who escaped communism and wept when justice finally came. I made them a promise: _not here. Not in America._
**I can 't keep that promise alone.**
The national Left is all in for her. I need to know you're all in as well – for the country we love, and for every family who crossed an ocean to be free in it.
Election Day is almost here, and what we raise now is what stands between her and the Senate. | | | If you've moved in the last year, Trump's new voter lists could have you down as living in the wrong state. And that’s why I said no to it.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142127092/655919065/-569431239?refcode=261025-moved&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxZTc1ZWViNi03M2QwLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=7n5LL3Zpm3RABVxox9Chii9j-PyhikNeoC9sTQ131T4=)
---
In March, Trump ordered the Department of Homeland Security to use federal records to build state-by-state lists of everyone eligible to vote. The privacy group suing to stop it pointed out the obvious problem: "Put simply: people move." About 7.1 million people moved to a new state in 2024. The IRS, Social Security and the Postal Service each know part of where people live. None of them knows it in real time. In court, the group put it plainly:**"No such comprehensive database exists anywhere at the federal level."** The timing makes it worse. Trump's order sends the lists to states at least 60 days before a federal election. Federal law says no state can require more than 30 days of residency to vote. **So anyone who moves inside that gap could end up listed in a state they've already left.** That could mean a college freshman who moved into a dorm in August, a nurse who took a job across the state line, or a retiree who moved to be near the grandkids. **The order doesn't tell states what to do with these lists. Some could use them to purge voters from their rolls weeks before Election Day. A federal judge could rule on them any day, but right now no court is stopping DHS from building them.** **[I won't accept a faulty federal spreadsheet deciding who still gets to vote, and I'm going to keep naming this for what it is. Can you chip in $15 right now to help my campaign fight back and mobilize a turnout too big to rig?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142127093/655919066/-569431239?refcode=261025-moved&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxZTc1ZWViNi03M2QwLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=7n5LL3Zpm3RABVxox9Chii9j-PyhikNeoC9sTQ131T4=)**

An Associated Press analysis of advance voting through Oct. 20 found turnout up double digits in most of the states that will determine Senate control, with Texas early ballots up 74% and Kansas more than doubling its 2022 pace. Hey team,
We are 9 days away from flipping PA-09.
Everything we've worked so hard to build has come down to this. We just need the resources to keep pushing.
**Here are 9 reasons to[ chip in $9](https://substack.com/redirect/bebec815-904b-4de1-96a3-d3b95ea28484?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to kick Dan Meuser out of Congress.**
1. Data Center Dan has bought and sold millions in AI stocks while voting to give data centers tax breaks and take away local control.
2. He's doubled his net worth in office.
3. His stock portfolio outperformed Warren Buffett's.
4. He's never held a real town hall.
5. He doesn't even live here.

You've heard Democrats talk about a "blue wave" this year. But what's really powering their Senate campaigns is a GREEN WAVE of cash. And it's crashing over the Senate map right now. Look at the latest FEC reports, covering July through September: ▶ **TEXAS** : James Talarico (D) raised $60.2 million. Ken Paxton (R) raised $10.2 million.
▶ **KANSAS** : Adam Hamilton (D) raised $9.4 million. Roger Marshall (R) raised $800,000.
▶ **GEORGIA** : Jon Ossoff (D) raised $33.1 million. Mike Collins (R) raised $2.8 million.

You may have seen headlines bragging about record Republican super PAC money. The GOP's top Senate super PAC just raised a record $272.9 million in a single quarter. Here's what those headlines leave out: **a super PAC dollar doesn't go nearly as far as a candidate dollar.** Federal law requires TV and radio stations to sell ad time to candidates at their LOWEST UNIT RATE in the final 60 days before a general election. That's the same rate the station gives its best commercial customer. Super PACs don't get that rate. They pay whatever the station charges. During a football game in Austin in September, a Republican super PAC was charged $450,000 to air a single ad. Talarico's campaign paid $50,000 for a spot in the same game, in the same market. **That's NINE TIMES the price.**

For years, the Left has built a national small-dollar machine. Liberal donors don't just give to candidates at home. They give to candidates in states they've never visited. Talarico has raised more than $122 million from individual donors this cycle, and more than $65 million of it came from small donors giving $200 or less. If James Talarico wins in Texas, it will be because of that mountain of small-dollar contributions. **[We need to use the same national model to fight back: direct contributions to our candidates.](http://links.stoppingsocialistdems.com/u/click?_t=4dcc2aab65fd4d0da6a107b0eef86d43&_m=53ebbea8f3fa45c282eb51f69a4ac90a&_e=BFouy-0UZsuUZPL9ylWg4HnD3oMzjGoo4oXcgPCrkFt7Vr2FFDhJsRNrvAcaR-DcdP5eSuFHU-hxyRjJpAA0hGzMw06Wu6t1jWjCniEOMFC6nNvaXT3lNr--DBvkeidlpEvSq0D1irKYP5HitdRM6-NUjw3QEvwqPRvnZ9GHEFr8VuHgHoWMnN8xDcKxKo0Elpm-hUZJO4jiDLq0mxzx0HeKUAcjnRi6BrU2eXZRzLtqV2rb7maojpqM5WMFq4hksdr7UOpvGTUSECVlWQczzay0zywVCVN3PHvkgT8ETNU2oEVAyvlm04XgHTVLUw7IsBbkC039bD5Z6fMvIlF-ZSB9Gdm6ZbgphRCRZIraXKt91_VkpFfV66wb5FJmlXd15hsiBT_iasc55mY7LtaTCA%3D%3D)** Once your money moves away from the candidate's own campaign, it buys less. But what's really powering their Senate campaigns is a GREEN WAVE of cash. And it's crashing over the Senate map right now. Federal law requires TV and radio stations to sell ad time to candidates at their LOWEST UNIT RATE in the final 60 days before a general election. That's the same rate the station gives its best commercial customer. Super PACs don't get that rate. They pay whatever the station charges. During a football game in Austin in September, a Republican super PAC was charged $450,000 to air a single ad. Talarico's campaign paid $50,000 for a spot in the same game, in the same market. name: Kailee Buller
subject: Peter, I need you on my side
body:
Every moment counts now.

| | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Peter,
We are now 9 days away from Election Day.
When I started this campaign, I said it would be built from the ground up by the people of Central New York. You've been part of that from the start, and I'm grateful.
**But these final days are when races like ours are won or lost.**
Every conversation with a neighbor, every reminder to a friend, and every yard sign in a front lawn matters more now than at any point in this campaign.
That is why I'm asking you to become an official VICTORY CAPTAIN for Kailee Buller for Congress.
[**YES, I'LL BE A VICTORY CAPTAIN >>**](https://us.list-manage.com/D1UGFRHHuiF?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
Here's what being a Victory Captain means...
Victory Captains are the people I'll count on most in the home stretch. You'll be the first to hear our closing plan, the first to get our final campaign updates, and the person your friends and family turn to when they want to know what's really at stake in this race.
_**We'll be counting on you to help make sure the people in your life have a plan to vote, to let us know who could use a yard sign, and to keep us in touch with what's happening in your corner of NY-22.**_
_**You'll be the reason voters who might have stayed home show up instead.**_
I'm running to lower costs, protect our communities, defend our farmers and small businesses, and make Central New York a place where our kids can build their futures. And I need people like you standing with me now, more than ever.
[ _So, Peter, will you be there?_](https://us.list-manage.com/wWi1LcTl6QO?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)

Every big fight with the federal government gets filed in one courthouse, because that's where the government lives. For twenty-five years, one judge there has kept drawing them.
His name is James Boasberg, and here's how he got the seat. George W. Bush put him on the D.C. Superior Court in 2002. Barack Obama elevated him to the federal bench in 2011 -- confirmed 96 to nothing. Chief Justice John Roberts put him on the FISA court in 2014, where he served as presiding judge from 2020 to 2021, and made him chief judge of the Alien Terrorist Removal Court from 2020 to 2025. Since March 2023 he has been chief judge of the district court itself.

name: Darline Graham
subject: Kamala's own words.
body:
This is what is at stake if Annie Andrews becomes a Senator |
---

_"The work that we can do about winning back the House and the Senate is going to be on a number of things. For example, I believe that we need to expand the Supreme Court."

"...we should be pushing for statehood for Puerto Rico and D.C., right?
-Kamala Harris_
Peter, take her at her word. We have 9 days to stop it.

This is what Democrats will do if they win the House and Senate.

_Pack the Supreme Court with liberal justices who will legislate from the bench._

_Add D.C. and Puerto Rico as the 51st and 52nd states to give Democrats extra seats in Congress._

_And you know they'll do whatever they can to bring back Roe v. Wade._

Friend,
Can you believe it? We’re officially 9 days away from Election Day! Before I share why these next few days are, hands down, the most important and consequential of the campaign, I want to take a moment to look back at where this all started — and how far we’ve come together.
**Where it all started:**
It all began with a simple idea: Kansans deserve a senator who actually listens to them. I never quite thought that I would run to become that senator. After all, I’m a pastor, not a politician.
But I decided to step up because I saw just how badly Washington’s chaos — and cruelty — was hurting the neighbors I love and the communities I serve.
I’ll be honest: I didn’t know exactly what to expect from a Senate race. But we hit the ground running and have come so incredibly far, all thanks to supporters like you.
**Where we are, days before Election Day:**
With 9 days until the big day, let me give you the lay of the land:
* The newest polls show us running neck and neck with Sen. Marshall — with some even giving us a narrow lead.
* Over the past several weeks, election experts have shifted our race further away from a “Safe Republican” rating, with RealClearPolling even calling Kansas a 50/50 TOSS-UP. _These shifts confirm that this race is going to be very close._
* The president’s super PAC just transferred $1 million to support Sen. Marshall, and the Senate Leadership Fund — a major GOP super PAC — announced they’re launching a $15 million ad buy to attack me.

These aren’t just numbers; they are proof that Kansas is ready for change.
When I look at these metrics — which all point to this being one of the most competitive races in the nation — I am filled with gratitude for folks like you. The truth is, no one expected Kansas to become a battleground. It’s only because of this grassroots team that we’re on the brink of making history.
Whether you phone-banked or knocked on doors or chipped in a few bucks or even just shared one of these emails with a friend, you are the reason our momentum is surging.
**Please don’t forget this: All the good we do in Washington will be thanks to you. That’s something to be immensely proud of.**
**Roger Marshall’s recent months:**
Roger Marshall’s deep ties to Florida were further exposed.
“Reporting by the Kansas City Star revealed Marshall took official trips from Washington, D.C., to Sarasota, spending more than $18,000 in taxpayer funds from 2021 to 2024. The trips reportedly stopped after a hurricane destroyed the area. It is unlawful for a senator to use taxpayer money for personal travel.”
There was an embarrassing rejection by voters at the Kansas State Fair debate on his “home turf.”
It’s clear Kansans are ready for a new voice in Washington.
**It all comes down to these final days.**
But right now, we find ourselves at a critical juncture. In a 50/50 toss-up race, it’s anyone’s game. It’s these last weeks that will determine who pulls ahead and whose momentum slips.
That’s why we’re gearing up, not slowing down. We’re preparing to air ads across Kansas to reach the final persuadable voters. We’re building a massive get-out-the-vote effort to ensure all of our voters have a plan to get to the ballot box.
But here is our biggest challenge: Sen. Marshall’s super PAC allies have already spent $23 million to crush our momentum, and they are gearing up to spend even more. The truth is that even our incredible momentum cannot withstand an attack this big without additional support. We need to fight back.
Here’s a little window into our campaign: Every single day, we make tough decisions on how much we can spend to reach voters based on the amount of support we receive from folks like you. **[That’s why I’m asking you to make a donation today.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142142473/655954633/-540544497?amounts=10,25,50,100,250&refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk895&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjYxMjYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiN2MzNjE5ZmMtN2FkMC1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAyMjQ4MjlmODY5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=2hjveFRq4nARWLrYstpA3E_KKGqNu89hYHThN9cJX-I=)**
With the stakes so incredibly high in these _make-or-break weeks_ , we truly need everyone to take an active role in this movement, in all the ways you’re able.

Under the Trump Administration, we’ve seen gross negligence and abuses of power from DHS when it comes to ICE. Recently, two suspected MS-13 gang members were hired by ICE and sent to federal law enforcement training. Nobody caught them until someone noticed their gang tattoos.

This is not a one-off. A career ICE official with 17 years at the agency, who ran the unit responsible for vetting new hires, filed a whistleblower complaint. He alleged that the Trump administration hired armed agents without completing their background checks. He warned of “grave national security risks” and an “unprecedented lowering of standards.”

**Why? To hit a goal of 10,000 new ICE agents, the administration dropped age limits, cut training short and fast-tracked applicants.**

We’ve seen what happens next. In Maine, an ICE agent with repeated domestic violence allegations shot and killed an unarmed man. A local official said that he had “too many red flags” to be hired by the town’s police department. **Too many red flags to be a police officer, but able to wield a deadly weapon with ICE.**

Far too many members of Congress today have never been middle or working class a day in their lives — and it shows in the policies they pass. **My story is different, and I think that’s a good thing. **
I’m not running for Congress to become “somebody.” I’m not asking for your vote to turn around and try to climb some political ladder in Washington.
**I’m running because I love this community, and I’m tired of watching politicians like Bill Huizenga put special interests and billionaires ahead of the people they’re supposed to represent. **
I was born and raised here in Michigan, a public school kid from modest roots and the son of a teacher. Growing up, our family had to make the small sacrifices that most families across Michigan know so well — putting off home repairs and stretching our grocery budget as far as it would go.
