I just heard about a complete Socialist lunatic running for Congress, and I need your help to keep him as far away from Washington as possible.
It’s Brandon Gill: I know you’re busy, so I’ll jump straight into it.
You and I have heard about big-government wackos before – politicians who think they should control every single aspect of your life: how you raise your kids, what you eat for dinner, what kind of car you drive, and how you power your home.
But I never thought one would actually stand a chance of stepping foot in Congress.
Take a look at this guy:
---
[](https://trk.emails.evansforcolorado._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmcmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW10cG9zaXRpb249MyZleF90aWQ9MjAyNjEwMjVfTkQtUzcuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDY5NTQzLTkyMDImdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPTIwMjYxMDI1X05ELVM3LjExMDExN190MjA2OTU0My05MjAyIn0/N0rFtoiN6aMDLrr5vXGDJw)
---
* He’s a vegan who calls farming "horrific" and thinks we should all be forced to eat tree nuts and legumes instead of real American beef.

* He actively campaigned alongside proud, self-proclaimed socialist Zohran Mamdani.

* He wants to ban fossil fuels and destroy our oil and gas industries.

* He believes YOU, the hardworking taxpayer, should foot the bill for transgender surgeries for minors.

The absolute power trip these left-wing politicians are on is disgusting.
If you know me, you know I’ve never been afraid to speak my mind. I believe the government should get off the backs of everyday Americans, and our leaders have a duty to protect our American way of life for generations to come.
Congress does NOT need any more radical Democrats – let alone an actual socialist.

body:
Twenty months ago, I announced that I was running to be the next Governor of Ohio.

| [](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.-N_Q)
---
Twenty months ago, I announced that I was running to be the next Governor of Ohio.
I remember saying that day that I believed Ohio’s best days were still ahead of us.
[After spending the last twenty months traveling to all 88 counties and talking with people across this state, I believe that even more today.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.-QoxGoeA)
---
[](https://trk.email.vivekforohio._wYAOA6BB6ry85OZ6DeQ)
---
| [FINAL STRETCH FUND: HELP VIVEK WIN](https://trk.email.vivekforohio._rW6g)
---
I’ve heard a lot along the way. People have told me about the businesses they’re trying to keep afloat, the bills that keep getting more expensive, and the kids they wish didn’t have to leave Ohio to find opportunity.
Those conversations have stuck with me. They’re a big part of why I want this job in the first place.
I want Ohio to be a place where it’s easier to build something, raise a family, and get ahead. Where we lower taxes, cut the red tape, keep our communities safe, and give the next generation a reason to stay.
[That’s what I signed up to fight for twenty months ago, and I’d be grateful if you’d help me see it through. If you can swing it, will you please chip in $10 to help me finish what we started?](https://trk.email.vivekforohio._Gb1Ru2y2YhCpTeZ5jw)
---
| [FINAL STRETCH FUND: HELP VIVEK WIN](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)
---
I’m asking now because we’ve reached the part of this race where every bit of help really does matter.**
**My opponent, Amy Acton, and her liberal allies are spending heavily to defeat us. And right now,[ this race is a coin flip.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.-dy3B4AIktHEeJcwEA)**
**We knew this would be a tough race, Peter. But we didn't put in twenty months of work to come up short in the final day.**
**I meant what I said when I got into this race. And I’m going to give everything I have between now and Election Day to keep that promise.**
**[I hope you’ll stick with me.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)**
**Gratefully, Vivek Ramaswamy

name: The Democrats
subject: January 3, 2027
body:
Where will we be in ten weeks? [ ](https://ak.democrats.org/go/87341?t=1&akid=10048%2E22930333%2EI8j2jm)
---
Derek, 10 weeks from today we'll be watching a new Congress get sworn in. **This could be a momentous day.** If Democrats are swept into office on a blue wave, January 3 will be the day that we begin setting our country on a new, _better_ path forward. But we need your help to make that happen. Every single community organizer, door-knocker, and campaign is relying on the momentum we build right now, and we can’t let them down. Keeping our momentum going and powering Democrats to victory up and down the ballot will require an influx of immediate support from our grassroots team. [**So we’re asking: Can you chip in $7 to the DNC today to help power Democrats to victory across the country and make sure that January 3rd is the start of a new, Democratic majority?**](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-october-2026-gfr.AWsDfI&refcode=em_20261025_10048_fr&amount=7&t=19&akid=10048%2E22930333%2EI8j2jm) **[DONATE $7](https://ak.democrats.org/go/89866?c0=em-dnc-october-2026-gfr.GS9qR7&amount=7&refcode=em_20261025_10048_fr&t=20&akid=10048%2E22930333%2EI8j2jm)** Derek, the stakes could not be higher. If the blue wave doesn’t land, or if Democratic momentum stalls at the last moment, January 3 could look very different. It _could_ be the start of another **two years** of an unchecked Trump administration. Without a Democratic majority to hold him accountable, _there’s no telling what he’ll do if he and his yes-men are given another two years to attack our democracy_. **This moment calls for bold action, and it starts with _all of us_ digging deep in these final 9 days before Election Day.** [**When you chip in $7 today, you’re investing in Democratic victories, protecting democracy, and securing the bright future our country deserves on Election Day.**](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-october-2026-gfr.AWsDfI&refcode=em_20261025_10048_fr&amount=7&t=21&akid=10048%2E22930333%2EI8j2jm) _If you 've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution instantly._ | | | **[Donate $7](https://ak.democrats.org/go/89866?c0=em-dnc-october-2026-gfr.GS9qR7&amount=7&refcode=em_20261025_10048_fr&t=22&akid=10048%2E22930333%2EI8j2jm)**

Friend, Chris Hayes asked me if I ever want to just “tap out.”
I receive so much hatred, vitriol, harassment, and threats on a daily basis. I’ve been attacked by the President, the Vice President, members of Congress, billionaires, foreign leaders, and more. Now I’m being targeted by a fascist government with no care for the truth or the law.**I understand why he would ask the question.**
But for me, this is simple. I got into politics to fight for my community, improve lives, and create the kind of country I know we can be. I do this because I believe deeply in Medicare-for-All, ending homelessness, strengthening workers’ rights, securing a quality education for every child, putting a stop to endless wars, and much more.
These goals — and the movement that fights for them — are my north star, and no amount of intimidation is going to stop me. I’ve been through much worse than dealing with a buffoonish failure like Trump.
So, I will remind you that we are almost one week from Election Day, which is our chance to strike at the heart of MAGA’s authoritarian takeover and win back power for the working people of America. I’m asking for your solidarity today as we fight clear-eyed for the future we believe in.

Peter,
Michiganders are already voting. Ballots have been sitting on kitchen
counters for weeks, and in-person early voting just opened across the
state.

That changes everything about how I think about the rest of this campaign.

Many people who are still making up their minds aren’t waiting until
November 3 to decide. They’re choosing *right now* who they want to be
Michigan’s next U.S. senator.

And every day we can’t get in front of these Michiganders is a day Mike
Rogers and his MAGA allies do it for us with baseless attacks and
fearmongering.

Then there’s today.

Donald Trump is in Port Huron this afternoon to try to rescue Mike Rogers.
Nine days before the election, Rogers needs the President of the United
States to fly in and hold his hand.

Trump has already gone after my name, my faith, and my family. Whatever he
says today, you can bet MAGA groups will cut it into attack ads by
tomorrow morning. Those attacks can’t go unanswered, not while voters are
holding their ballots.

So, a $10 donation today does two jobs at once:

1. It puts our message — getting money out of politics, putting more
money in your pocket, and passing Medicare for All — in front of an
undecided voter.
2. It helps us respond quickly to whatever Trump, Rogers, and their MAGA
network throw at us.

Hey, it's Ken Burns.
I'm reaching out today because in this moment of deep division in our country -- with extreme partisanship and callousness coming from Washington -- it is my deep conviction that our nation needs Adam Hamilton in the U.S. Senate.
**[Will you join me in supporting Adam Hamilton's Senate campaign?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/b90b2cce-b9f9-41ea-a96c-f8f59641abff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
I'm a student of history. I've studied our country's triumphs, our deepest divides and the moments that defined who we are as a nation. _We are approaching another such decisive moment this November._
**Will our country choose the path of partisan division? Or will we elect leaders with the moral courage to unite us again?**
Adam Hamilton is not a career politician; he's a listener, first and foremost. For over 30 years, he has served his community as a pastor with courageous, compassionate and effective leadership. Like so many of our most impactful leaders, Adam has stepped up to run when he saw Kansans hurting under the heartless policies coming out of Washington.
In a political era dominated by partisan noise, Adam brings the bridge-building we so desperately need in the Senate. He's focused on what actually matters: standing up for working people, lowering everyday costs and ending the chaos and corruption in Washington.
Right now, we have a historic opportunity in Kansas: Democrats haven't won a Senate race in Kansas in nearly 100 years, but now, it's a true electoral battleground, with experts calling this race a 50/50 toss-up.
**But our history teaches that progress is never guaranteed. It is fought for, protected and renewed by people choosing to step up when the stakes could not be higher.**
That's why I'm asking you to step up today. It's folks like you who make history. And especially in this tight Kansas race, it will come down to these final days before the election. So everyone must do their part. Our divisions will not heal themselves.
**[Will you make a donation of whatever you can afford to Adam's campaign for U.S. Senate in Kansas? This is a critical moment for our country, and I would not ask for your help if this were not so important.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/b90b2cce-b9f9-41ea-a96c-f8f59641abff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Donate](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/b90b2cce-b9f9-41ea-a96c-f8f59641abff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Adam and the movement building around his campaign give me hope. And that kind of hope -- in better politics, in a better future, in a world where the people have the power -- has always been the fuel of democracy.
Thank you for supporting Adam today.
Ken Burns

| | | Hello, friend. It's Hillary Clinton.

I'm reaching out because our democracy is at stake, and it’s critical that we act right now.

I've held many different roles throughout my life ‐‐ First Lady, senator, Secretary of State, presidential candidate going head‐to‐head with Donald Trump, mother, grandmother, American citizen, and more. Serving our country in so many ways has taught me so much. And so, I am _deeply_ concerned about the state of our nation under Donald Trump and GOP control.

**[If you're also worried and already know that we must take back the Senate to start fixing things, chip in $7 to the DSCC now.**](https://go.dscc.org/go/24212?amount=7&t=5&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&addr1=&addr2=&city=Cresco&state=Pennsylvania&zip=18326&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&ask=7&amounts=7%2C14%2C28%2C70&code=DPE-FD-20261025-HillaryClinton-HillaryClintonWorriedAsX-Pros-sl1&refcode=DPE-FD-20261025-HillaryClinton-HillaryClintonWorriedAsX-Pros-sl1&akid=27084%2E9716520%2EldHS2W)

Let me explain further: As the former Secretary of State, I'm horrified by how Donald Trump has handled foreign affairs ‐‐ he's slashed USAID and consistently bullied and belittled our closest allies.

As a former Democratic senator for New York, I'm disturbed by the Senate GOP's spinelessness in the face of Trump's actions. They seem more focused on currying favor than faithfully serving their country and those that elected them.

As a former presidential candidate, I'm ticked off to see Donald Trump's blatant disregard for the rule of law. I've spoken about his threats to democracy before, but his daily actions are beyond the pale.

As a mother of a wonderful daughter and a doting grandmother of three amazing kids, I'm disgusted by Donald Trump's horrific treatment of women and girls.

And as an American citizen, I'm fed up with how Donald Trump, aided by Senate Republicans, is trampling over our laws, values, and rights all while pushing an agenda that is gutting health care access and driving up costs for so many families ‐‐ all to give himself and his billionaire buddies tax breaks. Reproductive freedom, voting rights, even basic respect ‐‐ these things simply don't matter to him, and they simply never will.

The sad reality is that Donald Trump is neither willing nor able to step up and provide the leadership that our country needs, and Senate Republicans sure aren't stepping up either. It's up to us ‐‐ as Democrats ‐‐ to make a difference, and with the midterm elections just 9 days away, now is the time to act. **None of us can sit this out.**

[**History _will_ remember how we respond to this moment. subject: [Volunteer Opportunity] Just over one week left to reach voters
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft
body:
The Swing Left community is working hard to get out the vote.
#
Hi there,
With just over a week left until Election Day, the Swing Left community is working hard to get out the vote in swing districts and states across the country.
**Here’s a story from the field that we hope keeps you motivated to get out the vote in these final days:**
Earlier this month, Kevin, a Ground Truth volunteer, got on a bus to Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, to knock doors in a pivotal swing district that could decide control of the House.
Kevin admitted that canvassing doesn’t come naturally to him. He’s an introvert, and he hates the feeling of interrupting someone’s breakfast, nap, or football game. What made this Ground Truth canvass feel different was knowing he was there to listen—to meet the person in front of him with curiosity, awareness, and kindness.
While canvassing, Kevin met a postal worker on his route who told him he was “apolitical.” After handling campaign mail for both parties, he said he felt like none of the candidates got anything done and there was no difference between the parties.
Kevin could have launched into an argument. Instead, he got curious about the experience behind those words—about what it felt like to be unseen, unheard, or disrespected by both parties. They had a short conversation where Kevin and his husband, Chuck, listened and offered questions of curiosity before the postal worker had to get back on his route. But before they parted, he surprised Kevin by saying he might vote on Election Day.
**That’s what makes Ground Truth conversations different. The goal isn’t always to push to change someone’s mind. Sometimes, making a difference means making someone feel heard.**
And sometimes, showing up leads to an unexpectedly personal moment.
At Kevin’s last stop of the day, a woman answered the door, leaning on a cane while her gray terrier, Stormy, pulled excitedly at his leash. When Kevin explained why he’d come, she had one question: “Can you help me get a ride to the polls?”
Kevin said he’d make some calls.
But before they left, Stormy needed a walk. So Kevin and Chuck offered to take him across the street to the park. For fifteen minutes, there was no red or blue. Just a dog in a park, two volunteers walking and talking, and a woman who was grateful that someone had knocked on her door and taken the time to help.
Kevin eventually got her connected with a ride to the polls. She’s excited to vote on November 3rd.
**Two very different conversations. But both are reminders of what can happen when we show up with curiosity, kindness, and a willingness to listen.**
With our final weekend of canvassing coming up, the races that decide control of the House, Senate, and key governorships could come down to conversations like Kevin’s—and there’s still time to have conversations that could make a difference before Election Day.
[**If you’re looking for a way to get involved, click here to find the best volunteer opportunity for you based on where you live and what you like to do.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/3211?t=1&akid=3280%2E1562180%2ESWw0uv)
**[Take Action Now »](https://act.swingleft.org/go/3211?t=2&akid=3280%2E1562180%2ESWw0uv)**
No experience is necessary. We’ll train you and make sure you have everything you need to be successful!
We hope to see you at the doors!
The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. Kevin admitted that canvassing doesn’t come naturally to him. He’s an introvert, and he hates the feeling of interrupting someone’s breakfast, nap, or football game. What made this Ground Truth canvass feel different was knowing he was there to listen—to meet the person in front of him with curiosity, awareness, and kindness. While canvassing, Kevin met a postal worker on his route who told him he was “apolitical.” After handling campaign mail for both parties, he said he felt like none of the candidates got anything done and there was no difference between the parties. Kevin could have launched into an argument. Instead, he got curious about the experience behind those words—about what it felt like to be unseen, unheard, or disrespected by both parties. They had a short conversation where Kevin and his husband, Chuck, listened and offered questions of curiosity before the postal worker had to get back on his route. But before they parted, he surprised Kevin by saying he might vote on Election Day. That’s what makes Ground Truth conversations different. The goal isn’t always to push to change someone’s mind. Sometimes, making a difference means making someone feel heard. And sometimes, showing up leads to an unexpectedly personal moment. At Kevin’s last stop of the day, a woman answered the door, leaning on a cane while her gray terrier, Stormy, pulled excitedly at his leash. When Kevin explained why he’d come, she had one question: “Can you help me get a ride to the polls?” Kevin said he’d make some calls. But before they left, Stormy needed a walk. So Kevin and Chuck offered to take him across the street to the park. For fifteen minutes, there was no red or blue. Just a dog in a park, two volunteers walking and talking, and a woman who was grateful that someone had knocked on her door and taken the time to help. Kevin eventually got her connected with a ride to the polls. She’s excited to vote on November 3rd. Two very different conversations. But both are reminders of what can happen when we show up with curiosity, kindness, and a willingness to listen. With our final weekend of canvassing coming up, the races that decide control of the House, Senate, and key governorships could come down to conversations like Kevin’s—and there’s still time to have conversations that could make a difference before Election Day. No experience is necessary. We’ll train you and make sure you have everything you need to be successful! We hope to see you at the doors! The Swing Left Team Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power. Which future do you want to wake up to on November 4th?
#
Picture this, Peter:
It’s November 4, and Texas looks completely different. Which future do you want to wake up to?
**If Latino voters stay home:** Greg Abbott gets four more years of selling Texans out to his wealthy donors and tech billionaires. Corrupt Ken Paxton heads to the U.S. Senate, and South Texas stays stuck with Monica De La Cruz, a puppet who answers to Trump instead of the people she represents.
**If Latino voters show up:** With Gina Hinojosa, we’d _finally_ have a governor who works for Texans. James Talarico would take his fight for working families to the U.S. Senate. And Bobby Pulido would bring South Texas values to Congress. Our schools, our healthcare, and our paychecks would finally have leaders who back us up, and Texas would prove once and for all that Latino voters decide its future.
_**This is the year Texas can transform, but only if we turn out.**_
That’s why we’re on the ground across the state, knocking on doors, sharing accurate election information, and making sure every eligible Latino voter has what they need to cast their ballot.

Hi Peter, it’s Hannah Pingree.

Governor Andy Beshear invited me to introduce myself and explain why I’m running for governor of Maine — **and how I plan to stand up to Donald Trump.**

I’m a mom of two teenage kids from a small island off the coast of Maine. I’m also a former Speaker of the Maine House, school board chair, and director of Maine’s “Office of the Future” who has spent my career taking on difficult fights and delivering results - from building housing to fighting the climate crisis.

When I was Speaker of the House, Maine was the first state in the country to pass marriage equality and have it be signed into law by our governor. As lead co-sponsor of that bill in 2009, it wasn’t the easy or politically safe thing to do, but it was the right thing to do for families. So we brought people together, stood our ground, and won that fight.

**That’s how I’ve always approached public service and that’s the kind of governor I’ll be.**

This election underscores just how important the job of a governor is – protecting our rights, defending our values, and making sure families aren’t left to pay the price for the dysfunction in Washington.

Donald Trump is counting on governors to be intimidated by his threats, distracted by his chaos, or too divided to fight back.**I won’t be.**

When his administration attacks our rights, our health care, our schools, or the people who make Maine their home, I will use every tool available to fight back. I’ll speak out, take action, partner with other governors, and take it to the courts. And while Trump works to divide us, I’ll stay focused on making life more affordable, expanding opportunity, and delivering results for Maine families.

A note from Senator Ashley Moody |
---
Peter,
I'm going to be honest with you, because I don't know any other way to say this.
My heart breaks for France right now. City halls burning to the ground. More than 600 police officers injured in a single day. Rioters tearing the French flag off the monument to their own Republic – and raising a Palestinian flag in its place, while others march under the hammer and sickle.
Communists and radical Islamists, side by side in the streets. **That 's not a coincidence. That's an alliance.** And it has eyes on more than Europe.
This radical movement is working to infiltrate our own country – and it's counting on patriots like you not realizing it until it's too late.
It is the honor of my life to serve as Florida's U.S. Senator. My state is full of people who already know how this story ends. Families who fled Castro with nothing but the clothes on their backs. Venezuelans who watched their country get looted by socialists in a single generation. Nicaraguans who escaped Ortega. They came here because America was the one place it couldn't happen.
Here, that movement has a fellow traveler on the ballot, and her name is **Angie Nixon.**
She runs a bookstore called "Cafe Resistance." On its wall hang portraits of convicted cop killers – including Assata Shakur, who murdered a New Jersey state trooper and fled to Castro's Cuba. When she was confronted about it, she said she stands by "everything in this bookstore."
She closes her speeches with a line from the Communist Manifesto – "We have nothing to lose but our chains" – and she took that chant to a CAIR gala. She was one of just 7 votes against teaching students the history of communism. She signed the pledge to abolish ICE. She voted against tougher penalties for people who assault police officers.
And she just raised $7 million to take Florida's U.S. Senate seat – more than we raised in the same three months. And Bernie Sanders just pointed his $23 million war chest at this race and came to Florida himself to campaign for her and turn out the vote.
This is a special election – the biggest Senate race in the country this year – and some new polls say it's within the margin of error. If she wins, she becomes **the first dues-paying member of the Democratic Socialists of America in the U.S. Senate.**

subject: I was reflecting on Isaiah 59:19
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Van Orden for Congress
body:
This is spiritual warfare
| | When the enemy shall come in like a flood, the Spirit of the LORD will lift up a standard against him.
~ Isaiah 59:19
---
I'm sure I don't really need to tell you this, but we're in a spiritual battle. This isn't a game or some kind of hyperbole; the soul of our nation is on the line right now.
The other day, I read and reflected on Isaiah 59:19. The passage reads: When the enemy shall come in like a flood, the Spirit of the LORD will lift up a standard against him.
Unfortunately, sick and godless ideology is festering in our nation today. Liberal billionaires and coastal elites have bankrolled monsters in their scheme to take the House Majority and thrust America into chaos.
My Team and I are fighting to defend the House majority from these lunatics. If we fail in Congress, our nation will quickly fall to this insidious evil too.
Listen, I'm not going to tell you this will be easy. Protecting our Christian way of life, our children, and our shared values is a tall order. But this short excerpt from Isaiah reminded me that with the Lord on our side, we shall overcome all that stands against us!
No matter what my role was, from Navy SEAL to husband and father, I have always led with the light of Christ and that's not about to change when we defend the House in November. But I can't win this race without your prayers and support.

Hey folks,
I never thought I'd be sitting here agreeing with Marjorie Taylor Greene, but here we are.
She's absolutely tearing into Donald Trump over his broken promises, the Epstein files, and the possibility of another escalation in Iran. And the bigger story? The MAGA movement is starting to fracture from within. This is exactly the kind of opening we can't afford to ignore.
Here's what we get into:
* [**00:01:20**] Marjorie Taylor Greene calls out Trump's ridiculous $5,000 check promise and exposes the hypocrisy of Republicans suddenly embracing what they've spent years calling socialism.
* [**00:03:52**] Why Trump's promised checks are an act of political desperation while everyday Americans struggle with rising gas prices, groceries, and housing costs.
* [**00:05:26**] Greene unloads on Trump's broken campaign promises, the war in Iran, and the Epstein files. It's a brutal takedown from someone who used to be one of his loudest defenders.

Look, I'm not suddenly becoming a Marjorie Taylor Greene fan. We still disagree on plenty. clean_body: We need to elect progressive champion Justin Pearson to Congress as part of flipping Congress blue. | | | Friend, We’ve got a little over a week to take back Congress from racist Republicans. This month, I joined progressive champion Justin Pearson in Tennessee to help get him elected to Congress: Justin leads a local environmental justice group, where he helped cancel a dangerous oil pipeline and shut down a cancer-causing facility. Now he’s fighting against Elon Musk’s hyperscale data center in Memphis. If Justin joins me in Congress, we’ll fight corporate polluters together, push to end poverty and abolish ICE, and make sure that U.S. tax dollars fund Americans’ needs — not genocide. | After Justin protested for gun reform, Republican lawmakers expelled him from the state legislature, making him nationally known. He won back his seat in a special election with overwhelming support and continued fighting for the people — passing legislation to monitor corporate polluters and leading legislative fights for gun control, a higher minimum wage, and expanded voting rights and healthcare coverage. Justin decided to run for U.S. Congress in Tennessee’s only majority-Black and majority-Democratic district. But this spring, racist GOP state leaders split up that district as an attack on Black voters. Justin sued the state to block the new racist voting maps, and re-launched his campaign in the same place but in a new district. Now, the stakes are even higher because we need to win back Congressional representation for Black residents of Tennessee. And with redistricting, winning this seat means helping to flip Congress blue. As Democratic early voters in Tennessee are reporting problems with electronic voting machines that keep defaulting to Republican candidates, we urgently need to increase voter turnout. Let’s make sure Justin has the resources to reach voters and win. If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your secure donation will go through immediately, split evenly between Justin J. Pearson and Rashida Tlaib: | | | | | | | | | Republicans are interfering in this year’s midterm elections, undoing years of progress to try to destroy our multiracial democracy and keep white supremacist control of Congress. We won’t let them take away our power or our rights. Thank you for taking action to stop voter suppression and build a country and a world where everyone can flourish. With you in the fight for better, Rashida Rashida Tlaib for Congress PO Box 32777 Detroit, MI 48232 | Paid for by Rashida Tlaib for Congress | | Sent via . clean_body: I am not a career politician. I am stepping up to serve again because Montana is my home. | Fellow Patriot, Early voting is already underway in Montana. Election Day is 9 days away. I want to make sure you know exactly who is asking for your support in these final days. My name is Kurt Alme. I am a Montana native. I was born in Great Falls. My dad taught high school math. My mom was an elementary school teacher. Throughout my life, I’ve lived across the state from Dillon to Victor to Helena to Miles City. I’ve spent my entire career serving and protecting Montana families. As Montana’s Budget Director and Revenue Director, I spearheaded two of the largest tax cuts in state history, balanced our state budget, and helped make Montana debt-free. I’ll fight to do it again in Washington. As Montana’s U.S. Attorney, nominated by President Trump and confirmed by the Senate twice, we went after violent criminals, expanded drug prevention and treatment, and targeted drug traffickers all the way to the cartels – and tore them out by their roots. Last year my office prosecuted more criminals than any year in the last 20 years, and we drove down violent crime. **I am the only candidate in this race with deep Montana roots and a proven record of cutting taxes, balancing our state budget, and locking up violent criminals. I am not a career politician. I am stepping up to serve again because Montana is my home. I want our kids and grandkids to have an even better life than we have, with the same freedoms and values that we hold dear. President Trump has given this campaign his Complete and Total Endorsement. With less than two weeks left and votes already being cast, this race is in its final stretch. Every dollar raised right now helps us reach Montana voters before they make their decision. Thank you, - Kurt Alme Conservative for Senate FOLLOW KURT ALME ON SOCIAL MEDIA** | | Paid for by Alme for Senate Don't want to receive any more of our emails? We hate to see you go: .

name: The Turning Point Action Team
subject: It all starts with three states...
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY TURNING POINT ACTION (TPACTION
body:
Three states are about to decide a lot more than 2026.

| | | |
---
Friend,
---
We've looked at the polling in every swing state and swing race in the country. It's margin of error, either way, almost everywhere.

At this point, it's not about winning anybody over. _It's about who actually shows up._

If conservatives turn out in November, we'll win every critical battleground and lay the groundwork for victory in 2028 and beyond.

That's why Turning Point Action is focusing all our efforts on three key states: Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire.

**We call these states the new RED WALL.**

_Let us explain why they matter so much... _

After 2024, Charlie looked at the numbers, looked at the maps, and told our team something simple. If we lock down Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire, the Left's entire strategy falls apart. Their map collapses. Their path back to power disappears.

Here's why... Winning the presidency comes down to 270 electoral votes. Lose Arizona and most of the realistic paths to the White House in 2028 are gone. Lose Nevada and New Hampshire and the Left rebuilds the Blue Wall they lost in 2024.

Whoever wins in 2028 controls the 2030 Census. The Census drives redistricting. Redistricting sets the congressional map for the next ten years.

Fellow American, it's Michele Tafoya.

I've been on the road a lot recently, pressed for time, hopping from one city to the next, but I still wanted to take some time out of my day to write to you.I didn't waste time sending this to my team for final review; I wanted to get this over to you as soon as I possibly could.

If you've been following what's happening in Minnesota, here's where we're at now:
1. The latest polls now have me and my Far Left opponent, Peggy Flanagan, DEAD EVEN in the home stretch. Voters are clearly demanding change.
2. My campaign has been surging past our expectations thanks to thousands of grassroots patriots like you chipping in just $5 or $10 whenever they can (contrary to my socialist opponent's wealthy boosters).
3. The Democrat political machine has invested thousands in bogus attack ads in Minnesota against me because they're terrified of us pulling off the upset.

It's clear now, more than ever, that the tides are turning in our direction. I wanted to show you, in these points above, some of the fruits of all of our hard work together.
__But the final buzzer still hasn 't sounded, and you don't get a prize for winning the 3rd quarter when there's plenty of time left in the game!__
I've seen first-hand PLENTY of teams who think they've got the win in the bag take their foot off the gas and go on defense... all to face defeat right before the clock hits zero.
**We won 't be that team.**
If anything, we're itching to snatch victory from the jaws of defeat. We've known since the start of this movement that we're the clear underdog in this race.

I’m writing to you and a small group of folks for a specific reason: you’ve been with us on this campaign, but you haven’t made your first contribution yet.*
I know money’s tight for a lot of Nevada families right now. I relied on WIC and food stamps while raising my first son as a single dad, so I know what it means to count every dollar.
**But as we get ready to kick off the final full week of this campaign, I could really use your support.**
MAGA Republicans are pouring money into ads attacking me, and we have to answer them while reaching the undecided voters who will decide this race. The polls are clear: if we reach those voters, we will win. **The only thing standing in our way is the resources to do it.**
**[Will you chip in your first $5 today to help us answer the attacks and reach undecided voters in these final days?](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20261025_1_ak.OppO79&amount=5&refcode=em20261025-1165&t=3&akid=1179%2E127862%2EK-nWBA)**

Aaron

**THE HOME OFFICE IN WAHOO, NEBRASKA ([The Daily Whatever Press](https://substack.com/redirect/cf126269-3255-423c-9bd3-e5267128b05e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))**--With nine days left before the midterms, the good news has piled up so high that seven slots couldn't hold it anymore, so we're doing nine.
David Letterman's Top Ten lists used to arrive "from the home office in Wahoo, Nebraska," and I'm borrowing the office because Nebraska is suddenly one of the places Republicans are sweating. Letterman got 10. We get nine, one for every day left on the calendar, and every one of them was built, gold-plated brick by gold-plated brick, by Donald Trump.
I'm a bona fide GenXer, which means optimism is not my factory setting. I don't trust good news until it's been counted, certified, and left on my porch in a box.
But even I have to admit the numbers this week are fucking gorgeous.

## No. 9: Trump's approval rating has reached spelunking depth
Reuters/Ipsos has him at 31%, his lowest ever. CNN has him at 32%, also his lowest ever. NYT/Siena, with 3,494 likely voters, has him at 36%. Gallup had him at 44% at this point in 2018, the year Democrats picked up 41 House seats, so he's running eight to 13 points behind the version of himself that already lost the House once. Yowza.
On cost of living, AP-NORC puts his approval at 17%. This is the man who promised voters he'd end inflation starting on day one, and he now polls like the last donut in the break room at 4 p.m. if that donut's glaze was flaking off and losing its damn mind at rallies, fantasizing about all the other hot, sexy man donuts.
[Leave a comment](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=222059485&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&isFreemail=true&comments=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIyMDU5NDg1LCJpYXQiOjE3OTI5NDczNjUsImV4cCI6MTc5NTUzOTM2NSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.ugYQruxsRoVBeCwpIHaYuSYP2DIbJzU4gb1hj4iVBmA&r=1hvr60&utm_campaign=email-half-magic-comments&action=post-comment)
## No. 8: The generic ballot is showing off
NYT/Siena has Democrats ahead 52% to 41% on the generic congressional ballot. CNN has it 49% to 39%. The Strength In Numbers/Verasight poll has Democrats up 12 among likely voters, with Republicans stuck at 41% among registered voters, the lowest the GOP has ever scored in that poll.
In 2018, Democrats won the national House vote by about eight and a half points, and Nancy Pelosi got her gavel back. We are polling ahead of that, and I would like everyone to stay calm about it while I scream into a throw pillow.
Trump's ratings on immigration, border security, and deportations also hit new lows in the Verasight poll, and Republicans no longer lead Democrats on immigration or deportations at all. He spent 10 years building his entire political brand on one issue, and he's lost it. Oh, honey. I'd feel bad, except that schadenfreude is just so much more fun.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=222059485&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIyMDU5NDg1LCJpYXQiOjE3OTI5NDczNjUsImV4cCI6MTc5NTUzOTM2NSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.ugYQruxsRoVBeCwpIHaYuSYP2DIbJzU4gb1hj4iVBmA)
## No. 7: Democrats are the ones who can't sit still
Pew Research Center found that 63% of Democratic supporters say they're extremely motivated to vote, against 46% of Republican supporters. Half of Democrats have given the election "a lot" of thought; only 36% of Republicans can say the same.
In October 2022, Republicans led on both measures. Four years ago, the enthusiasm gap was theirs. Now it's wearing our jersey and asking where to park.

Nine days, nine reasons to grin, and one job left for you. Polls have been nice to us before. | | and | Oct 25| | | ∙| | Preview ---|---|--- | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- | | ---|---|--- THE HOME OFFICE IN WAHOO, NEBRASKA ( nine days left before the midterms, the good news has piled up so high that seven slots couldn't hold it anymore, so we're doing nine. David Letterman's Top Ten lists used to arrive "from the home office in Wahoo, Nebraska," and I'm borrowing the office because Nebraska is suddenly one of the places Republicans are sweating. Letterman got 10. We get nine, one for every day left on the calendar, and every one of them was built, gold-plated brick by gold-plated brick, by Donald Trump. I'm a bona fide GenXer, which means optimism is not my factory setting. I don't trust good news until it's been counted, certified, and left on my porch in a box. But even I have to admit the numbers this week are fucking gorgeous. Blue Amp Media is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support our work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. No. 9: Trump's approval rating has reached spelunking depth Reuters/Ipsos has him at 31%, his lowest ever. CNN has him at 32%, also his lowest ever. NYT/Siena, with 3,494 likely voters, has him at 36%. Gallup had him at 44% at this point in 2018, the year Democrats picked up 41 House seats, so he's running eight to 13 points behind the version of himself that already lost the House once. Yowza. On cost of living, AP-NORC puts his approval at 17%. This is the man who promised voters he'd end inflation starting on day one, and he now polls like the last donut in the break room at 4 p.m. if that donut's glaze was flaking off and losing its damn mind at rallies, fantasizing about all the other hot, sexy man donuts. No. 8: The generic ballot is showing off NYT/Siena has Democrats ahead 52% to 41% on the generic congressional ballot. CNN has it 49% to 39%. The Strength In Numbers/Verasight poll has Democrats up 12 among likely voters, with Republicans stuck at 41% among registered voters, the lowest the GOP has ever scored in that poll. In 2018, Democrats won the national House vote by about eight and a half points, and Nancy Pelosi got her gavel back. We are polling ahead of that, and I would like everyone to stay calm about it while I scream into a throw pillow. Trump's ratings on immigration, border security, and deportations also hit new lows in the Verasight poll, and Republicans no longer lead Democrats on immigration or deportations at all. He spent 10 years building his entire political brand on one issue, and he's lost it. Oh, honey. I'd feel bad, except that schadenfreude is just so much more fun. No. 7: Democrats are the ones who can't sit still Pew Research Center found that 63% of Democratic supporters say they're extremely motivated to vote, against 46% of Republican supporters. Half of Democrats have given the election "a lot" of thought; only 36% of Republicans can say the same. In October 2022, Republicans led on both measures. Four years ago, the enthusiasm gap was theirs. Now it's wearing our jersey and asking where to park. clean_body: Nine days left. I’ll keep this short. | = I know your inbox is full right now, so I’ll get right to it. = Here’s why this matters. Ballots have been in CA-45 mailboxes for almost three weeks, and with nine days left, a lot of voters are filling theirs out this weekend. The conversations our volunteers have at the door right now are some of the last chances we get to reach them before they decide. Every one of those conversations depends on what we raise. It pays for the organizers who train volunteers, the walk lists that send them to the right doors, and the phone banks reaching voters we can’t get to in person. Two years ago, this race was close enough that it took 22 days to call. I don’t want to wake up on November 4th wondering whether we did everything we could. body:
Young voters are abandoning the GOP — we can offer them something better.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20261025-1&t=1&akid=4188%2E587540%2EHtkOuK)
Peter,
A couple years ago, plenty of people were convinced our party had lost a generation of young people, in particular young men, for good.
But the New York Times just ran the numbers, and the story looks _very_ different. In 2024, 55% of young men supported Trump. 31% of young women did as well. Today, they’re swinging back towards Democrats.
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261025_1_nyt.qRTMEq&refcode=em20261025-4188&t=2&akid=4188%2E587540%2EHtkOuK)
I’ll be honest, I’m not surprised. Young people who voted for Trump were promised lower costs, and what they got in return was skyrocketing gas and grocery prices and an illegal war nobody asked for. **Young voters know they’ve been sold a lie.**
But walking away from the GOP doesn’t mean they’re automatically coming to our side either.
**The truth is, if we want to earn this generation’s vote permanently, we can't just rely on the GOP’s failures as our talking points. We have to offer them courageous leaders they can actually trust and believe in.**
Leaders who will address the cost of living head on and root out the corporate PAC money that’s corrupted our politics. Leaders who will give them a real reason to believe things can get better.
That’s exactly why Leaders We Deserve exists. We’re backing and electing the next generation of bold progressive candidates to Congress and state legislatures across the country who will fight relentlessly for young voters, and understand the struggles they’re facing because they’re living them too.
**And the clock is ticking.** With 9 days left until Election Day, many of our endorsed candidates’ races will come down to a handful of ballots. Turning out young voters could be the difference between breaking the GOP’s grip on power and another round of the same broken promises.
That’s why next week I’m traveling to Ohio to host rallies on college campuses with our candidate Kristina Knickerbocker, who is running to flip a competitive red-to-blue congressional seat.
**[Will you pitch in $5 today to help our endorsed candidates reach young voters in these final days and flip red seats blue across the country?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261025_1_nyt.qRTMEq&refcode=em20261025-4188&amount=5&t=3&akid=4188%2E587540%2EHtkOuK)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261025_1_nyt.qRTMEq&amount=5&refcode=em20261025-4188&t=22&akid=4188%2E587540%2EHtkOuK)**
Thank you,
David Hogg

Louise Lucas is not a household name, nor should she be. State Senators from Virginia should barely make headlines within our own Commonwealth let alone in the newspapers of 49 other states (or a few territories, but I don't count them. In fact, I would relinquish them all tomorrow, but that's another subject. One day I'll write about my time appointed by W to the President's Task Force on Puerto Rico's Status). This week the octogenarian powerbroker state Senator was unceremoniously arrested, along with several members of her family, in a DOJ takedown of a crime family, and Louise Lucas made news.
The world is healing.
I won't give the nasty, vulgar, corrupt, scumbag Lucas much more thought here. She is unworthy, and I hope prison is hell for her and her reprobate gangster thug family, but Lucas is a springboard for me to opine on something larger: the elected leaders of the poor, and how, by and large, they are pure evil. If you go through the worst districts (in terms of crime, poverty, drug addiction, unemployment, homelessness, etc.) they are represented by some of the worst people in Congress.
Let me start with Charlie Rangel.
Charlie Rangel is dead. So is my uncle. The former represented Harlem in the U.S. House of Representatives for nearly 50 years. My uncle was NYPD Blue, and one of his jobs as a young cop in the early 70's while he was attached to the infamous 28th Police Precinct was delivering a wad of cash to The Honorable Charlie Rangel monthly. And Charlie, the nasty, vulgar, corrupt, scumbag that he was, would count it in front of him and laugh about how he was untouchable.
* * *
* * *
## The Capitalist is a reader-supported publication, we exist for you, because of you!
[Support What We Do](https://substack.com/redirect/64380d88-2f27-4444-a823-819e94ebf0dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* * *
True story? I don't know. Family lore, like Elizabeth Warren's Cherokee cheekbones or Kamala Harris' cry for "Fweedom" from her baby stroller. If I run for office (that's another op-ed in the works... hold your horses) this story won't be central to my appeal. I don't, however, see why my uncle would concoct such a story. He had plenty of others which were verifiable, as all cops do. But that story always stuck with me, especially when I got to DC 25 years ago and started working in politics, and Charlie was still causing trouble with endless phlegm stuck in his throat.
Here's Charlie, here's Harlem. Here's Charlie's wealth, here's Harlem. Here's Charlie who combined four apartments into a palatial spread all while claiming stabilized rents, here's Harlem. Here's Charlie, censured for **[dodging taxes](https://substack.com/redirect/ffce6caa-6e5b-43ea-92a9-26b5c40eff33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on a Dominican Republic estate sale, here's Harlem. Here's Charlie's **[$2.5 million net worth](https://substack.com/redirect/2d193356-6d7f-48d0-a659-d0f381758cd2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** at the time of his death, here's Harlem. Here's Charlie's estate **[claiming only $300,000](https://substack.com/redirect/64914d08-b0d5-4820-8bd4-4a9a6ab8f831?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** wealth to avoid taxes even in death.
And here's Harlem.
Harlem, which after decades of Charlie's tenure, is pretty much as dangerous, as dirty, as poor, with schools as terrible, and opportunities as scarce as ever. Harlem was good to Charlie, but Charlie was not good to Harlem. That power dynamic wasn't an accident. It was essential.
What's the expression? Rest in piss? Is that harsh? I've lost perspective.
The Virginia state senator is cut from the same cloth. The district she has represented since 1992 is the poorest, the most dangerous, has the worst schools, and has the least opportunity. It is not a coincidence. Lucas needs poor, hopeless, dependent people to stay in power. Someone wants to build a data center? Hell, no. Lucas won't allow it in her district. A data center could bring jobs and opportunity, but outside of her orbit. People with jobs and their own money don't need powerful elected officials for their bread, and no one would be beholden to Lucas... so no data centers. But she does love pot. Lucas led the charge to legalize pot in Virginia, and wouldn't you know it her family opened the first pot stores. Lucas is the pot Queen of Virginia.
Wonder if her stores took EBT?
Maxine Waters is 88 years old, and has represented Compton, California since 1991. She lives in Beverly Hills, in a **[$4.5 million home](https://substack.com/redirect/ef90d20b-c681-4697-8568-cbe697174c4e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , and has a net worth of $20 million. How is Compton doing? As well as Hampton Roads, Virginia? As well as Harlem, New York?
House minority leader Hakeem Jeffries lives in Prospect Heights, Brooklyn. Think 5 story brownstones, with large stone stoops, and 100-year old trees. He represents East New York and Brownsville, perhaps the most dangerous part of New York City. These are parts of Brooklyn where you don't stop at red lights, and if you have a car accident, you keep on driving. The vast majority of the residents are on welfare and in government housing projects. I'd be curious to do a video there on a random Tuesday at noon just to show how many able-bodied men are hanging out... but I wouldn't risk it. No joke. I would not risk it. No wonder why Hakeem doesn't live there.
The list of districts goes on and on, at the state and federal level. Districts gerrymandered to get all black or black majority demographics which elect black democrats who rubberstamp a progressive agenda. And the districts never improve. Never.
Never.
The people are trapped there. Jobs don't come in. Business don't open. Schools don't improve. Gang violence thrives. Violence is so common that it never makes the news. A shooting? A stabbing? Don't expect NBC news to send a camera crew. It happens every day.
I am well aware someone will call me racist. Yawn. That just means I am over the target... but the real racists are those elected officials who benefit from the misery of their constituency. The real racists are those with power to affect change, but who know the real change that will improve lives, and will reduce their power. So, they talk about climate change. Or Ukraine.
Free Palestine, or something.
Joe Biden put it best in the 2012 election when he warned a black audience "Mitt Romney is going to put you all back in chains".
Mitt Romney. Milquetoast, moderate, Mormon missionary Mitt is going to put black people "back in chains". Joe Biden is a racist, but you likely already knew that. See, Joe Biden needs black people to be poor, to be dependent. Joe Biden had to scare black people into being afraid that only he could keep them safe.
In his 2016 campaign, Donald Trump told black audiences that after generations of supporting democrats nothing in their life had improved. He asked for their vote **[saying](https://substack.com/redirect/9162111e-56db-4173-b967-e66818d94421?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** "what the hell have you got to lose?" Simple and effective.
It isn't just black America. It's poor America, writ large. West Viriginia is one of the poorest states in the nation, and one of the whitest. I guess there is a common denominator if you look at the last 50 years of its Senators: Jennings Randolph (democrat), Robert Byrd (democrat), Jay Rockefeller (democrat), Joe Manchin (democrat). It wasn't until this decade West Viriginia elected a Republican.
It's not just black America. It's democrat America: an entire party sustained by the misery of its constituents. Once people have jobs, have income, have prosperity and autonomy, and start questioning their taxes and scrutinizing their government, suddenly elected officials have a difficult job justifying their purpose let alone why they should be reelected. A prosperous people do not need government. Moreso, a prosperous people begin to eschew and curtail government, and that is a death sentence for democrats.
Term limits could help. Ending racial gerrymandering could help. In the case of Louise Lucas, prison will definitely help. But no amount of studies or white papers or seminars, no amount of angry op-eds like this, can do anything so long as elected officials can benefit off the poverty of others. They demand we tear down statues or push DEI quotas, yet the modern democrat is the real slave owner, keeping poor people, both black and white, on their district plantation forever.
Rest in piss. All of them.

That just means I am over the target. | | | Oct 25 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- The Capitalist exists because of you, and we want to hear from you! Louise Lucas is not a household name, nor should she be. State Senators from Virginia should barely make headlines within our own Commonwealth let alone in the newspapers of 49 other states (or a few territories, but I don't count them. In fact, I would relinquish them all tomorrow, but that's another subject. One day I'll write about my time appointed by W to the President's Task Force on Puerto Rico's Status). This week the octogenarian powerbroker state Senator was unceremoniously arrested, along with several members of her family, in a DOJ takedown of a crime family, and Louise Lucas made news. The world is healing. I won't give the nasty, vulgar, corrupt, scumbag Lucas much more thought here. She is unworthy, and I hope prison is hell for her and her reprobate gangster thug family, but Lucas is a springboard for me to opine on something larger: the elected leaders of the poor, and how, by and large, they are pure evil. If you go through the worst districts (in terms of crime, poverty, drug addiction, unemployment, homelessness, etc.) they are represented by some of the worst people in Congress. Let me start with Charlie Rangel. Charlie Rangel is dead. So is my uncle. The former represented Harlem in the U.S. House of Representatives for nearly 50 years. My uncle was NYPD Blue, and one of his jobs as a young cop in the early 70's while he was attached to the infamous 28th Police Precinct was delivering a wad of cash to The Honorable Charlie Rangel monthly. And Charlie, the nasty, vulgar, corrupt, scumbag that he was, would count it in front of him and laugh about how he was untouchable. The Capitalist is a reader-supported publication, we exist for you, because of you! True story? I don't know. Family lore, like Elizabeth Warren's Cherokee cheekbones or Kamala Harris' cry for "Fweedom" from her baby stroller. If I run for office (that's another op-ed in the works... hold your horses) this story won't be central to my appeal. I don't, however, see why my uncle would concoct such a story. He had plenty of others which were verifiable, as all cops do. But that story always stuck with me, especially when I got to DC 25 years ago and started working in politics, and Charlie was still causing trouble with endless phlegm stuck in his throat. Here's Charlie, here's Harlem. Here's Charlie's wealth, here's Harlem. Here's Charlie who combined four apartments into a palatial spread all while claiming stabilized rents, here's Harlem. Here's Charlie, censured for on a Dominican Republic estate sale, here's Harlem. Here's Charlie's at the time of his death, here's Harlem. Here's Charlie's estate wealth to avoid taxes even in death. And here's Harlem. Harlem, which after decades of Charlie's tenure, is pretty much as dangerous, as dirty, as poor, with schools as terrible, and opportunities as scarce as ever. Harlem was good to Charlie, but Charlie was not good to Harlem. That power dynamic wasn't an accident. It was essential. What's the expression? Rest in piss? Is that harsh? I've lost perspective. The Virginia state senator is cut from the same cloth. The district she has represented since 1992 is the poorest, the most dangerous, has the worst schools, and has the least opportunity. It is not a coincidence. Lucas needs poor, hopeless, dependent people to stay in power. Someone wants to build a data center? Hell, no. Lucas won't allow it in her district. A data center could bring jobs and opportunity, but outside of her orbit. People with jobs and their own money don't need powerful elected officials for their bread, and no one would be beholden to Lucas... so no data centers. But she does love pot. Lucas led the charge to legalize pot in Virginia, and wouldn't you know it her family opened the first pot stores. Lucas is the pot Queen of Virginia. Wonder if her stores took EBT? Maxine Waters is 88 years old, and has represented Compton, California since 1991. She lives in Beverly Hills, in a , and has a net worth of $20 million. How is Compton doing? As well as Hampton Roads, Virginia? As well as Harlem, New York? House minority leader Hakeem Jeffries lives in Prospect Heights, Brooklyn. Think 5 story brownstones, with large stone stoops, and 100-year old trees. He represents East New York and Brownsville, perhaps the most dangerous part of New York City. These are parts of Brooklyn where you don't stop at red lights, and if you have a car accident, you keep on driving. The vast majority of the residents are on welfare and in government housing projects. I'd be curious to do a video there on a random Tuesday at noon just to show how many able-bodied men are hanging out... but I wouldn't risk it. No joke. I would not risk it. No wonder why Hakeem doesn't live there. The list of districts goes on and on, at the state and federal level. Districts gerrymandered to get all black or black majority demographics which elect black democrats who rubberstamp a progressive agenda. And the districts never improve. Never. Never. The people are trapped there. Jobs don't come in. Business don't open. Schools don't improve. Gang violence thrives. Violence is so common that it never makes the news. A shooting? A stabbing? Don't expect NBC news to send a camera crew. It happens every day. I am well aware someone will call me racist. Yawn. That just means I am over the target... but the real racists are those elected officials who benefit from the misery of their constituency. The real racists are those with power to affect change, but who know the real change that will improve lives, and will reduce their power. So, they talk about climate change. Or Ukraine. Free Palestine, or something. Joe Biden put it best in the 2012 election when he warned a black audience "Mitt Romney is going to put you all back in chains". Mitt Romney. Milquetoast, moderate, Mormon missionary Mitt is going to put black people "back in chains". Joe Biden is a racist, but you likely already knew that. See, Joe Biden needs black people to be poor, to be dependent. Joe Biden had to scare black people into being afraid that only he could keep them safe. In his 2016 campaign, Donald Trump told black audiences that after generations of supporting democrats nothing in their life had improved. He asked for their vote "what the hell have you got to lose?" Simple and effective. It isn't just black America. It's poor America, writ large. West Viriginia is one of the poorest states in the nation, and one of the whitest. I guess there is a common denominator if you look at the last 50 years of its Senators: Jennings Randolph (democrat), Robert Byrd (democrat), Jay Rockefeller (democrat), Joe Manchin (democrat). It wasn't until this decade West Viriginia elected a Republican. It's not just black America. It's democrat America: an entire party sustained by the misery of its constituents. Once people have jobs, have income, have prosperity and autonomy, and start questioning their taxes and scrutinizing their government, suddenly elected officials have a difficult job justifying their purpose let alone why they should be reelected. A prosperous people do not need government. Moreso, a prosperous people begin to eschew and curtail government, and that is a death sentence for democrats. Term limits could help. Ending racial gerrymandering could help. In the case of Louise Lucas, prison will definitely help. But no amount of studies or white papers or seminars, no amount of angry op-eds like this, can do anything so long as elected officials can benefit off the poverty of others. They demand we tear down statues or push DEI quotas, yet the modern democrat is the real slave owner, keeping poor people, both black and white, on their district plantation forever. Rest in piss. All of them. Daniel Turner is the founder and executive director of Power The Future, a national nonprofit organization that advocates for American energy jobs. He also runs a sheep and cattle farm in rural Virginia. Did you see this?Trump just announced a new White House Women’s Health Task Force – and he put RFK Jr. in charge of it. _Yes, really._ Here’s my honest take on what this move means for women’s health:** ****It’s insulting – and worse, it’s dangerous. ** This is the same RFK Jr. who doesn’t believe in the HPV vaccine, which prevents cervical cancer in women. He also spreads misinformation about the science, effectiveness, and benefits of most other vaccines, too. He blocked teen pregnancy prevention funding, gutted maternal healthcare research, pulled us out of the World Health Organization, and defunded Planned Parenthood. **_And this is the same administration that has spent the last two years systematically dismantling the programs and research that keep women healthy. Now, just days before the midterm elections they’re terrified of losing, they want us to believe they care about women’s health? _** Last year, Republicans made the largest cuts to healthcare in our nation’s history, throwing more than 10 million people off Medicaid and spiking premiums for many millions more. All to bankroll $4.5 trillion in tax cuts for billionaires and massive corporations. Oh, and they carefully orchestrated the bill’s timing so its most brutal impacts take effect _after_ the midterms, when it’s too late to hold them accountable at the ballot box. Right here in Minnesota, we’re facing _double-digit increases_ in our health insurance premiums next year. But back to this bogus “task force” – I actually went to medical school. I spent more than 20 years caring for women as an OB-GYN physician. And I can tell you: this is not what investing in women’s health looks like. We don’t need a task force led by someone who is actively harming women’s health. We need to elect leaders who will invest in the research, our care, and our futures. **There are just nine days until Election Day, so if we’re going to send a clear message that we won’t accept this anymore, I have to ask: will you chip in today to power my re-election campaign through the final push? Here’s my honest take on what this move means for women’s health: It’s insulting – and worse, it’s dangerous. This is the same RFK Jr. who doesn’t believe in the HPV vaccine, which prevents cervical cancer in women. He also spreads misinformation about the science, effectiveness, and benefits of most other vaccines, too. He blocked teen pregnancy prevention funding, gutted maternal healthcare research, pulled us out of the World Health Organization, and defunded Planned Parenthood. And this is the same administration that has spent the last two years systematically dismantling the programs and research that keep women healthy. Now, just days before the midterm elections they’re terrified of losing, they want us to believe they care about women’s health? Last year, Republicans made the largest cuts to healthcare in our nation’s history, throwing more than 10 million people off Medicaid and spiking premiums for many millions more. All to bankroll $4.5 trillion in tax cuts for billionaires and massive corporations. Oh, and they carefully orchestrated the bill’s timing so its most brutal impacts take effect after the midterms, when it’s too late to hold them accountable at the ballot box. Right here in Minnesota, we’re facing double-digit increases in our health insurance premiums next year. But back to this bogus “task force” – I actually went to medical school. I spent more than 20 years caring for women as an OB-GYN physician. And I can tell you: this is not what investing in women’s health looks like. We don’t need a task force led by someone who is actively harming women’s health. We need to elect leaders who will invest in the research, our care, and our futures. Seems like a straightforward task, but when you throw in the $6 million Donald Trump has dumped into the district and the millions Mike Johnson’s PAC is spending, too, it gets a lot harder. The truth is, we’re being drowned out. Unless we pick up our fundraising — like, today — we’re not going to be able to reach those undecided voters. They’re going to hear Trump’s message instead. So the path to victory is clear: boost our resources and get our message in front of those undecided voters. I’ve got the second part, but I need your help with the first. = = | | | Thanks for sticking with me, Marie Gluesenkamp Perez = = | | | | | ---|---|---|--- Congresswoman Marie Gluesenkamp Perez represents Washington’s 3rd Congressional District. A fifth-generation Washingtonian, Marie built an independent auto repair and machine shop from the ground up with her husband, Dean. They live with their son in rural Skamania County in a house they built themselves. Marie for CongressPO Box 1164 Washougal, WA 98671 United States | | | | | Paid for by Marie for Congress

body:
A surge of grassroots support right now could transform this race and bring us one seat closer to retaking the House.
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/9?t=1&akid=41618%2E3422442%2EeToRGx)
Peter,
Democrats too often overlook places like Northwest Arkansas, but we can win there when candidates show that they will fight for working families and reject corporate PAC money.
**That’s exactly what Robb Ryerse is doing in Arkansas’ 3rd Congressional District, and why I’m proud to endorse his campaign.**
I’ll explain more about why I’m backing Robb, but first, **[I hope you’ll split a donation of $5 between his campaign and Truth to Power today.](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20261025_1_ak.HsLUX7&refcode=em20261025-41618&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=41618%2E3422442%2EeToRGx)**

Like Robb, I first ran for Congress to flip a Republican district by rejecting corporate PAC money and fighting relentlessly for everyday people. I know firsthand that these progressive values are a winning strategy.
Back in 2018, Robb even visited my district to help turn out voters, giving us the boost we needed to win. _Now, it’s our turn to return the favor and show up for him._
[](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20261025_1_ak.HsLUX7&refcode=em20261025-41618&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=41618%2E3422442%2EeToRGx)
Robb believes we need a government that works for us when we need it most. Unlike his opponent—who represents corporate donors and defense contractors— _Robb is running to represent the people._
While Republicans want to bury their heads in the sand, we have the opportunity to build political power that will help us deliver huge wins like Medicare for All and real accountability for corporate greed.
Donald Trump’s disastrous policies are driving up costs for everybody from California to Arkansas. **People all across the country, in red and blue districts, are feeling the squeeze. That gives candidates with strong progressive values like Robb the chance to win.**

This report comes on the heels of a bipartisan group of Secretaries of State and election officials around the country warning that the "biggest threat" to election security right now "is the federal government."

clean_body: I understand how to win statewide in a purple state — and I know Cindy can do it | | | | = | | | | Peter, Last November, Virginians made me the first woman elected governor in the Commonwealth's 400+ year history. On election night, when my husband Adam told our daughters, "Your mom is going to be the Governor of Virginia," I felt it in my bones. Other women forged the path for me, and I’m showing the girls and young women I’ve met that they, too, can achieve anything. But it hasn’t been easy. When I first ran for office, I had to work hard to flip a red congressional district everyone said was unwinnable. And in a purple state like ours, I had to bring together people of all stripes to build a winning coalition. So let me tell you: I know what it takes for a woman to win a tough race in politically contested territory. And when I look at Cindy Holscher, the Democratic nominee for governor of Kansas, I see a woman who’s putting in the work to do the same thing in another purple state. She’s running neck-and-neck with her MAGA extremist opponent Ty Masterson — and if she can win, she’ll show her own daughters, and all the young women who come after her, that they have a chance to lead, too. But Cindy’s race is so close, and national Republicans have poured in almost $20 million to run ads attacking her record. = | | | | | | = | | | Here's what I know from the governor's chair: when a woman wins statewide, she doesn't just add a seat to a party tally; she changes what everyone in her state believes is possible. Women governors have to build coalitions nobody handed us, and it makes us better at the actual job of governing: bringing people together, delivering commonsense wins, and keeping extremism out of the way of ordinary life. I'd like nothing more than to watch Cindy Holscher become America’s next woman governor, and show her own daughters the lessons I’ve shown mine. ****

**3.** Deb’s Republican opponent is bankrolled by many of Trump’s TOP supporters in New Mexico and is focused on bringing Trump’s extremism to New Mexico.

That’s why you’re hearing from us again — because what happens right now will shape what we’re able to do in the final stretch. Fellow American, it's Michele Tafoya.

I've been on the road a lot recently, pressed for time, hopping from one city to the next, but I still wanted to take some time out of my day to write to you.I didn't waste time sending this to my team for final review; I wanted to get this over to you as soon as I possibly could.

If you've been following what's happening in Minnesota, here's where we're at now:
1. The latest polls now have me and my Far Left opponent, Peggy Flanagan, DEAD EVEN in the home stretch. Voters are clearly demanding change.
2. My campaign has been surging past our expectations thanks to thousands of grassroots patriots like you chipping in just $5 or $10 whenever they can (contrary to my socialist opponent's wealthy boosters).
3. The Democrat political machine has invested thousands in bogus attack ads in Minnesota against me because they're terrified of us pulling off the upset.

It's clear now, more than ever, that the tides are turning in our direction. I wanted to show you, in these points above, some of the fruits of all of our hard work together.
__But the final buzzer still hasn 't sounded, and you don't get a prize for winning the 3rd quarter when there's plenty of time left in the game!__
I've seen first-hand PLENTY of teams who think they've got the win in the bag take their foot off the gas and go on defense... all to face defeat right before the clock hits zero.
**We won 't be that team.**
If anything, we're itching to snatch victory from the jaws of defeat. We've known since the start of this movement that we're the clear underdog in this race.
But we're FAR from throwing in the towel.

subject: We’ve come so far
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=9761%2E582294%2EyLW0L2 ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=9761%2E582294%2EyLW0L2 ]Chris Pappas for Senate

I wanted to
take a moment to reflect on how far we’ve come.

But if you don’t have time to read a longer message and want to show your
support, [ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261025_2.KgWtHp&refcode=em20261025-2&t=1003&akid=9761%2E582294%2EyLW0L2 ]please chip in $5 or any amount today.

I didn’t enter public service from a family of career politicians. My
roots are right here in Manchester, shaped behind the counter at my
family’s landmark restaurant.

Growing up working there taught me the value of hard work, accountability,
and serving our community. That’s the exact work ethic I wanted to bring
to Washington to fix a system that no longer works for everyday people.

Now in one of the most critical Senate races in the country, I’m ready to
keep being a voice for all Granite Staters.

We’ve come so far building a true grassroots movement across New
Hampshire, but the contrast in this race could not be clearer.

Our campaign is built by working people pitching in what they can when
they can, while John Sununu is backed by Donald Trump, MAGA billionaires,
and corporate PACs.

Sununu has sold out Granite Staters to corporate special interests like
Big Pharma and Wall Street and grew his net worth up to $35 million.
Granite Staters can’t trust him to fight for them as long as he can line
his own pockets.

With just 9 days left until Election Day, everything comes down to this
final stretch. I need your help to make sure we have the resources to
reach every last voter so we can protect this open seat and flip the
Senate blue in November.

body:

# Grateful for you
### This fight has been powered by people like you.
| | | [Gina Hinojosa](https://substack.com/@ginafortexas)
---
| Oct 25
---
| [](https://substack.com/@ginafortexas)
---
Hi -- sorry to interrupt your weekend.
I wanted to send a quick note to express how grateful I am for you.
**Thank you so much for being in this fight with us.** I genuinely mean that. Since we launched this campaign a year ago, it's been powered by people like you, and I couldn't be more proud of that.
I know how crowded your inbox must be at this point in the election year. Plenty of politicians are sending urgent emails while they have millions sitting safely in the bank.
That's not us. Greg Abbott is outspending us 10 to 1, which means that for every $1 we spend, Abbott is able to spend $10. That's a huge deficit we have to make up. If we don't raise enough, we face the very real threat of going dark on the airwaves.
But thanks to you and your support, this is one of the closest Texas governor's races in a generation. We are effectively tied in the polls, and no one knows what's going to happen come November 3rd.
**[I believe we can win this race. I feel it in my bones. But only if we have the resources to stay on the air and on the doors through these last 9 days to Election Day. Will you help me keep the momentum going by chipping in $10 or more today?](https://substack.com/redirect/d266de8d-ed6a-4c96-9e05-c26bbe0a9183?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Thank you thank you thank you.

Thank you for having my back, again and again.| | | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142172321/656029431/-1530659900?amount=25&refcode=261025_sherrod_jared&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlODgxZThjZi1hOGQwLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=R8QO2dVtzz1A6vAAJm-SFcBjWgeN_iLNa9X0ou3SJl0=)
