| | | Donald Trump took the stage in Highland Heights, just outside of Cincinnati. He droned on about my opponent (if you heard what he said, you know what I mean) and attacked _**“Jared Brown.”

**_ **The name you’re looking for is Sherrod Brown. And in 17 days, I’m going to be Ohio’s next U.S. Senator.**

Look, at this point we can expect all sorts of nonsense at these MAGA rallies – and we're getting it. It’s clear that Donald Trump is taking any chance to spew lies and deceive voters to get guys like my opponent over the finish line.

But my name isn’t the only thing that Donald Trump got wrong at his rally today. He’s missing the entire point. Public service isn’t supposed to be about theatrics. It’s supposed to be about making a meaningful difference in people’s lives.

Ohioans see more money going out the door, and not enough money coming in. Gas and diesel prices are through the roof. The same pill in the U.S. costs double what it does in another country. Data centers are devouring our water and energy while Ohioans are left to foot the bill.

It’s no shock that Trump spent this rally trying to distract from real issues – issues he's had a heavy hand in creating. His accomplishments for working families or a plan to solve any of these issues? Nonexistent. He doesn’t have any record to talk about, so his rallies are packed to the brim with lies and nonsense.

Donald Trump spent the afternoon fear mongering, making up stories, and distracting, distracting, distracting. I’ll tell you now: Donald Trump has no authority to promise every American $5,000 if Republicans hold onto the Senate chamber.

To Donald Trump and Jon Husted, serving in office is just about power. If you scratch my back, I’ll scratch yours.

We need leaders who will fight to unrig this system. Right now, we’re left with Jon Husted and Donald Trump in charge.

These Trump attacks tell us that Trump is worried about us flipping this seat. He wouldn't bring Ohio up, lob attacks my way, and try to boost my opponent if he didn't think it would work out for him. So that means we have to stay focused.

**I’ll conclude this on a more hopeful note, since I’m sure you didn’t want to spend your Monday morning reading about the latest bizarre comments from Donald Trump.**

The other side is counting on schemes, outside money, and empty promises to win. You and me? We’ll win the right way – by sharing our message with as many Ohioans as will hear it.

The data shows time and again that our campaign has the momentum we need. If we can sustain it for the next 17 days, we will flip this seat. That’s the challenge ahead of us now, and it’s a big one. We’re up against $317 million of Republican spending from Elon Musk, Peter Thiel, and dark money groups. We’re never going to be able to match them dollar for dollar, but we can do enough to keep this race competitive and spread the word far and wide.

When thousands and thousands of people get involved, the effect is so much greater than one super PAC or Trump rally.

**[I’m grateful to have you on board. If you’ve already gotten involved in this campaign, thank you. If you haven’t yet and are waiting for the best time, I hope you’ll take this as your sign to donate to my campaign and Equal Opportunity Now. Every donation, door knocked, or conversation will put us closer to winning this.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142172322/656029432/-1530659900?refcode=261025_sherrod_jared&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlODgxZThjZi1hOGQwLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=R8QO2dVtzz1A6vAAJm-SFcBjWgeN_iLNa9X0ou3SJl0=)**

| Peter,
Louisiana is MAGA's death star. It is the place where they test their most insidious policies before firing them off at the rest of the country.
This summer alone, they canceled an ongoing election under a fake "state of emergency" and eliminated one of our majority-Black Democratic districts.
They passed a bill forcing homeless people into indentured servitude. They criminalized abortion. They deployed the National Guard into our streets. They tortured immigrants at the Winn Correctional Center in North Louisiana.
But a rebellion is brewing in the Bayou.
A catastrophic vulnerability has been found in MAGA's death star, and we are about to blow it wide open. Trump's approval rating in the state is underwater. Voters are fed up with the foreign wars, an economy on the brink of collapse, and National Guard and ICE storm troopers patrolling our own streets.
The rebellion has already struck. On May 16th, Democrats turned out in record numbers and delivered a blow that blindsided MAGA, sinking every single one of Governor Landry's amendments by 20 points or more.
Now Democrat Jamie Davis just outraised MAGA candidate Julia Letlow last fundraising quarter and is statistically tied with her in the latest poll on the U.S. Senate race.
Losing Louisiana would be a catastrophic defeat for MAGA in the very state they built as their death star. And winning this Senate seat could all but guarantee Democrats flip the chamber. That is a move that could save the republic.
We need every Democrat to rally to this cause. We might not get another shot at an upset like this. Where do you think your tax dollars belong?
Maybe you're concerned about funding your kids' public schools, preserving Colorado's National Parks, or making sure our seniors get the care they need.
Maybe you notice roads near you need work, or small businesses and farms in your area are struggling to make ends meet. Maybe you think tax dollars could be directed there.
**Well, Donald Trump has other ideas about how to spend your money, and it's vanity projects and forever wars. **
**He would rather spend your tax dollars on a ballroom to throw parties for his billionaire friends or host a cage fight at the White House than invest them back into our communities where they belong.**
**_It's sickening. _**
Congressman Jason Crow here. I'm not about to sit by and watch as Donald Trump plays fast and loose with our wallets in the name of his own ego. Especially not when he's lining his and his friends' pockets at the expense of hardworking folks just trying to pay the bills. Especially not when lives are at stake.

body:
With Republicans pouring in millions in this final stretch, that kind of money has the potential to make a difference.
#
Hi there,
Election Day is just 9 days away, and there are signs of shifting momentum everywhere: The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (the arm of the Party that focuses on the House of Representatives) has expanded its battlefield to 92 districts, and independent analysts at the _Cook Political Report_ recently shifted 29 House races toward Democrats in just two days.
In response, Trump’s super PAC is spending millions across 66 races to try to rescue Republicans—and Trump himself is traveling to states like Texas and Alaska to try to stop the bleeding.
**That being said, we can’t take a single state or district for granted. With Republicans pouring in millions in this final stretch, that kind of money poses a real threat in swing districts.**
That’s why the Immediate Impact Fund is currently focused on the 20 Congressional races—12 House and 8 Senate—where your donation will make the biggest difference in swinging the national balance of power in these final days. But there’s not much time left for grassroots donations to make an impact.
[](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=immediate-impact-2026.DM5m6O&utm_source=ak&%3Butm_medium=em&%3Butm_campaign=iif-2026&%3Butm_content=20261025-2&%3Brefcode=ak_em_iif-2026_20261025-2&t=1&akid=3281%2E1562180%2E_68mal)
Right now, campaigns are deciding on their final TV ad buys, how much they can spend on digital ads, and even whether they can afford one more round of pizza for volunteers. Without help, they risk being drowned out just as voters are casting their ballots.
[**That’s why we’re asking you to donate $25, or any amount that makes sense for you, to the Immediate Impact Fund today.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=immediate-impact-2026.DM5m6O&amount=25&%3Butm_source=ak&%3Butm_medium=em&%3Butm_campaign=iif-2026&%3Butm_content=20261025-2&%3Brefcode=ak_em_iif-2026_20261025-2&t=3&akid=3281%2E1562180%2E_68mal)
**[Donate $25 »](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=immediate-impact-2026.DM5m6O&amount=25&utm_source=ak&utm_medium=em&utm_campaign=iif-2026&utm_content=20261025-2&refcode=ak_em_iif-2026_20261025-2&t=23&akid=3281%2E1562180%2E_68mal)**
In Senate races, your donations will support Mary Peltola in Alaska, Josh Turek in Iowa, Adam Hamilton in Kansas, Troy Jackson in Maine, Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, Scott Colom in Mississippi, Chris Pappas in New Hampshire, and Sherrod Brown in Ohio.
And in House races, your donations will support Bill Hill in Alaska (AK At-Large), Amish Shah in Arizona (AZ-01), Randy Villegas (CA-22) and Marni von Wilpert (CA-48) in California, Christina Bohannan (IA-01) and Lindsay James (IA-02) in Iowa, Sean McCann (MI-04) and Christina Hines (MI-10) in Michigan, Cait Conley in New York (NY-17), Brian Poindexter in Ohio (OH-07), Bob Harvie in Pennsylvania (PA-01), and Bobby Pulido in Texas (TX-15).
Each of these candidates is facing a huge wave of outside spending in these final weeks, and your support today can help ensure they have the resources to respond and get their message out to as many voters as possible.
Thank you, as always, for everything you do,
The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20261025-2&t=24&refcode2=3281_1562180__68mal&akid=3281%2E1562180%2E_68mal)

The Constitution is clear on that. But this Secretary’s complete lack of respect for the law is putting American lives at risk. So as a 20-year Navy veteran, I’m running to win this seat back and stand up for servicemembers in Washington. Here in Hampton Roads, when Washington talks about resuming combat, it’s talking about sailors who live down the street and families who know that means an empty chair at the dinner table. **There are 9 days until Election Day.** This race is a Toss-Up. Democrats need to flip just three seats to win back the House, and with it, the power to demand answers, hold hearings, and insist on a vote before any president sends our servicemembers into harm’s way. clean_body: | = | | ="Should orders and the law ever conflict, our officers must obey the law.” That line hangs on a plaque at West Point. It reminds the men and women of our Armed Forces that America’s servicemembers don’t “just follow orders.” They follow the Constitution. The Secretary of Defense clearly didn’t get the memo. This week, Pete Hegseth flew to the Middle East, unannounced, as talk grows of restarting the war with Iran. That decision belongs to Congress. The Constitution is clear on that. But this Secretary’s complete lack of respect for the law is putting American lives at risk. So as a 20-year Navy veteran, I’m running to win this seat back and stand up for servicemembers in Washington. Here in Hampton Roads, when Washington talks about resuming combat, it’s talking about sailors who live down the street and families who know that means an empty chair at the dinner table. There are 9 days until Election Day. This race is a Toss-Up. **We call these states the new RED WALL.**

_Let us explain why they matter so much... _

Whoever wins in 2028 controls the 2030 Census. The Census drives redistricting. Redistricting sets the congressional map for the next ten years.

This midterm decides which way that goes.

Peter, Election Day is just nine days away. Before we ask you to **[chip in $3](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142173215/656032443/-1807803310?refcode=em-10.25.26-all-b&amount=3&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDE1MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNmU1ZjVhYy1hZWQwLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=-ZGFkTAdggSjdSTih8ezu9H7gxazipFR9i2m2bOTnoY=)** , here are three reasons this race matters:
1. In 2024, George flipped this seat from Republican control. This is his first re-election, and Republicans want this seat back.

**Not great news for voters, Team** _:_ Just weeks before the pivotal midterm elections, **Texas election officials discovered that an unknown number of voter registration applications have not been processed** due to an error by the Texas Department of Public Safety. According to an email sent to county officials and provided to Votebeat, DPS failed to send the applications, which were submitted by voters through its online driver’s license portal, to county voter registrars for processing. **This DPS portal is a major voter registration channel in Texas.** From 2020 through 2024, about 6 million Texans used it to register to vote, according to testimony DPS officials provided to state lawmakers in 2025. _Texas has more than 18 million registered voters._ This is where you come in -- Wherever you live, we have voter tools that you can use. **[Verify your registration, find out where to vote, get election reminders, and more](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142173728/656034208/1044253134?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAwNy8xLzg5MjE1IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjQ2NTk1MWE4LWFmZDAtZjExMS1iZjViLTAwMjI0ODI5Zjg2OSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=AMUkbcVTW5rnBX5xdjoia_00etkgR9y4cBxv2KdVJkE=&emci=5229559d-84d0-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&emdi=465951a8-afd0-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&ceid=33603084)**. **Voters in Texas** can check their status with our tools, on the [**Texas Secretary of State’s website**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142173729/656034210/864965444?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAwNy8xLzg5MjE1IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjQ2NTk1MWE4LWFmZDAtZjExMS1iZjViLTAwMjI0ODI5Zjg2OSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=AMUkbcVTW5rnBX5xdjoia_00etkgR9y4cBxv2KdVJkE=&emci=5229559d-84d0-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&emdi=465951a8-afd0-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&ceid=33603084#/login), at a county election office, or by mail.

Dream In the go-big-or-go-home collective consciousness of Texas, no
ambition is deemed too reckless, no daydream too wild. Save perhaps one.
It is the idea, fantastical to many as it is irresistible to others, that
the Democrats will win a statewide race in Texas for the first time in 32
years. According to the latest New York Times/Siena University poll of the
race for U.S. Senate, James Talarico, a 37-year-old state legislator seen
by national Democrats as one of the breakout stars of this cycle, is ahead
of his Republican rival, Ken Paxton, the state’s scandal-plagued attorney
general, by six points. The poll was conducted from Sept. 21 to Sept. 30.
A survey from mid-September, the ReconMR/Siena Research Institute poll,
also showed the Democratic gubernatorial candidate, Gina Hinojosa, four
points ahead of the three-term G.O.P. incumbent, Greg Abbott, the most
dominant political figure in Texas. Cue the fluttering heartbeats. Cue, as
well, the eye-rolls. Given how thoroughly Republicans have dominated the
state, and how the hopes of Democrats have repeatedly crashed, some Texas
pollsters remain skeptical. “At some point, you do get conditioned by all
that’s happened in the past,” said James Henson, the director of the
University of Texas at Austin’s Texas Politics Project. “I mean, you look
at the trends and you have to admit that something’s going on. But you
still don’t want to believe your lying eyes, because you’ve been burned
for so long.” Mr. Henson was referring to the perennial spectacle of
much-ballyhooed Texas Democratic aspirants face-planting against the Lone
Star State’s red wall. First came Tony Sanchez Jr., the swaggering and
self-funding Laredo oilman whom Gov. Rick Perry dispatched in 2002 by an
18-point margin. Next was the state senator Wendy Davis, who attracted
worldwide attention for her filibuster in the Texas Legislature against an
anti-abortion measure but whom Mr. Abbott demolished by 20 points in 2014.
Finally, the El Paso congressman Beto O’Rourke came up 2.6 points short of
defeating Senator Ted Cruz in 2018 but then suffered a 10-point loss to
Mr. Abbott four years later. Even with the awareness of such humiliations,
Democrats find themselves maintaining that 2026 could, at long last, be
the year. President Trump’s deep unpopularity and the prospect of a blue
wave could, they insist, extend into the state he won by nearly 14 points
in 2024. According to a September survey conducted by Texas Southern
University, Mr. Trump is seven points underwater in Texas. Mr. Talarico
has run an energetic and well-financed campaign, while Mr. Paxton has
staged far fewer public events and has had to rely on outside groups to
fund an attack-ad blitzkrieg against his Democratic opponent. Mr. Abbott,
meanwhile, has outspent Ms. Hinojosa by a 10-to-one ratio, yet has been
unable to build an insurmountable lead. “People have vastly underestimated
Gina,” said Ms. Davis, now a political consultant and a senior adviser to
Planned Parenthood Texas Votes, an advocacy organization. “Dollar for
dollar, she’s running the best statewide campaign we’ve ever seen.” Such
optimism stands in defiance of the political axiom that Texas is where
idealistic Democrats go to be mugged by reality. The party’s demise there
is not a product of ill fortune, Mr. Henson said. “Governor Abbott has
built an impressive election machine that has benefited state-level
Republicans again and again for a decade and a half,” he said. “And the
Democratic machinery here is almost nonexistent.” A ‘Hollowing-Out’ I have
written about the politics of my native state at regular intervals for
more than three decades. After watching the Democrats’ century-long rule
in Texas come to a decisive end with Gov. Ann Richards’s loss to George W.
Bush in 1994, I saw the party descend into atrophy in which failure begot
more failure. “The 30-year drought has done a lot of things,” said Luke
Warford, the chairman of the Travis County Democratic Party and the
founder of the Agave Democratic Infrastructure Fund. “It’s kept donors on
the sidelines, which makes a lot of potentially good candidates not run
because there’s no belief they can win. And it also makes a lot of really
talented staff leave to find better-paying work in true battleground
states.” The Democratic Party has no counterpart to Mr. Abbott, and hasn’t
since 1993, when Senator Lloyd Bentsen moved to Washington to join
President Bill Clinton’s cabinet. Its weaknesses are even more glaring
farther down the hierarchy. In recent elections, as many as one-third of
state races have gone uncontested by Democrats. One-fifth of the party’s
county chairs and two-thirds of its precinct chairs have been left
unfilled. Until last year, the state party had a negative operating
budget. As the veteran Democratic consultant Matt Angle observed, “There’s
been a hollowing-out of the party.” Still, those of us who recall the
satisfied sense of invincibility among Texas Democrats after roughly a
century of one-party rule have detected similar signs of overconfidence
among the state’s ruling party. The party’s rightward tilt, increasingly
forceful with each legislative session, reached its apotheosis in March,
with Mr. Paxton’s primary victory over the more moderate Republican
four-term incumbent, Senator John Cornyn. Mr. Paxton, a close ally of Mr.
Trump’s, was impeached by the Republican-controlled State House (and later
acquitted by the State Senate) in 2023 over allegations that included
bribery. He was also accused by his wife of adultery. Mr. Trump endorsed
him anyway, all but guaranteeing his landslide primary triumph over Mr.
Cornyn but in the process testing the allegiance of center-right Texans.
In similar fashion, the Texas G.O.P. is in danger of losing many Latino
voters who voted for Mr. Trump in 2024 after years of siding with
Democrats. “We adopted a lazy way of campaigning that bit us on the ass,
and we’ve learned from that,” Mr. O’Rourke said. “Now it’s the Republicans
who’ve gotten really lazy and complacent and comfortable.” Signs of
Republican Overreach Simply spending one week driving through the vastness
of Texas, as I did in September, is all it takes to appreciate an underdog
party’s uphill battle. The state’s 32 million residents are spread across
20 media markets, many of them distinct ecosystems, from the urban colossi
of Houston and the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex to the oil patch of the
Texas Panhandle to the Latino-dominated borderlands of the Rio Grande
Valley. “When national donors are deciding where to invest, they look at a
place like Iowa, where $5 million can fully fund a race,” said Katherine
Fischer, the director of the Texas Majority PAC, which was established by
the liberal philanthropist Soros family. “That’s why Texas is always at
the bottom of their list. It’s just so damned big.” Reaching so many
markets presents a daunting challenge for an upstart candidate like Ms.
Hinojosa, a state representative from the border city of Brownsville.
“There’s still 20 percent of the electorate that doesn’t know who I am,”
she said in an interview in mid-September. To date, Ms. Hinojosa’s
campaign has said that it has raised about $20 million. For his part, Mr.
Talarico spent about $30 million earlier this year to introduce himself
statewide as a man of Christian faith and a member of the Texas House with
a record of supporting bipartisan legislation. Since that time, however,
Mr. Paxton and his associates have invested more than $100 million in an
effort to redefine his opponent as “radical” and “weird,” with ads that
quote from remarks Mr. Talarico made several years ago (and later
renounced) suggesting that “God is nonbinary” and that there are six
biological sexes. Mr. Paxton and his allies have at times questioned Mr.
Talarico’s manhood and even his Christianity, an effort to jolt the
sensibilities of a state prone to mythologizing godly and masculine
archetypes. “How they’re negatively defining Talarico is kind of a
bank-shot way of saying that he’s not a true Texas conservative,” Mr.
Henson said. Whether money can overwhelm conditions on the ground is the
riddle looming over the Texas races. In the border city of Laredo, which
Mr. Trump won in 2024 — the first time a Republican had done so in over a
century — signs of buyer’s remorse are evident. Arrests by Immigration and
Customs Enforcement agents in Laredo were higher in July than in any other
American city. Mr. Trump’s erratic trade policies have further created
instability at the city’s port of entry. While acknowledging the economic
concerns that many border residents share, Adrian Zapata, a business
executive in the health industry who voted for Mr. Trump in 2024, said in
an interview that the negative ads against Mr. Talarico were resonating
with some of his family members. “They see Talarico as an ultraliberal,”
he said. “They’re done with the ‘they/them.’ They’re going to vote for
Paxton just because of that.” As for Mr. Zapata, “I’m not ready to vote
for Talarico,” he said. “But I don’t like Paxton. He’s never done anything
for South Texas, and his personal and business dealings have hurt him a
lot with folks down here.” There is a similarly muddled electoral picture
in the cattle country of deep West Texas adjacent to Big Bend National
Park. Mr. Trump and Mr. Abbott have aggressively championed a border wall
and artificial intelligence data centers, both of which threaten to
disrupt the region’s pastoral ethos. A coalition of more than 200
landowners has sued the federal government over the border wall, while
other residents have circulated a petition to protest the construction of
a new data center near Fort Stockton. George Johnson, a cattle feed
operator in Alpine, waved off such concerns, saying: “Folks worrying about
data centers were also worried when the internet got started. It’s
Talarico who scares me to death, him and all that socialist talk.” Others
in this largely conservative region harbor the view that Republicans have
failed to make good on their promises. Thaddeus Cleveland, the Republican
sheriff of Terrell County, said that both he and his county had voted for
Mr. Trump in 2024, but added, “Everything he campaigned on, we’re seeing
the opposite of, like going to war.” Sheriff Cleveland predicted that the
negative campaign ads by the Republicans would not factor as significantly
into the votes of his neighbors as “the price of groceries and gas, which
are compounded here because we’re so far from everywhere else.” But it is
in purple Tarrant County, dominated by Fort Worth, where the party could
pay the price for having potentially overestimated its mandate from the
voters. Conservative leaders have cut funds for nonprofits that aid
at-risk children, subjected school library books to right-wing litmus
tests and eliminated free bus rides to polling stations in poor
neighborhoods. “The far-right leaders here have implemented Project 2025
on a county level,” said Alisa Simmons, a Democrat and county commissioner
who is running to unseat the conservative county judge, Tim O’Hare. In an
early sign this year that area Republicans may be out of step with Tarrant
County’s constituents, a Democratic aviation machinist and union leader,
Taylor Rehmet, defeated Leigh Wambsganss, a well-funded Republican
Christian activist who led the conservative takeover of several metroplex
school boards. He won by 14 points in a January special election for a
State Senate seat covering a region that Mr. Trump won by 17 points in
2024. A ‘Gradualist’ Theory Which party prevails in Texas is a complicated
riddle. Historically a low-turnout state — it ranked second to last in the
2024 election, ahead of only Arkansas — Texas held a primary in March that
saw nearly one in four voters showing up to the polls, a modern record for
midterm participation, with Democrats slightly outpacing Republicans. A
few factors could conspire to thwart a blue wave in Texas. As of 2020,
straight-ticket voting is no longer possible in the state, which could
impact the mostly Democratic urban counties where that practice has
frequently been used by voters in past elections. Texas is one of only
eight states that lack universal online registration, while voting by mail
is also highly restricted. In January, Mr. Abbott turned over the state’s
list of approximately 18.7 million registered voters to the Trump
administration, and 1.2 million of them have subsequently been put on the
“suspense list” because their addresses have not been verified. The recent
shuttering of nearly one-third of Tarrant County’s polling sites by its
Republican-controlled county commission is particularly worrisome for
Democrats. “The reason we’ve lost these statewide races in the past is
because we’ve never gotten enough out of Tarrant County to overcome the
margins in rural Texas,” Ms. Davis said of the turnout. “If we don’t get
it to 53 or 54 percent this November, it’s game over. James and Gina can’t
win.” But the state’s Republicans have reasons of their own to be fretful.
Partly because of the recruitment efforts of the Texas Majority PAC and
Blueprint Texas, a down-ballot candidate support organization co-founded
by Ms. Davis earlier this year, the Democrats are fielding a full slate in
all 150 state races for the first time in a half-century. Though many of
these aspirants face long odds, their presence on the ballot could
energize the Democrats in predominantly conservative regions who have not
bothered to turn out in the past. “If we win on Nov. 3, most of those
names running down-ballot in really tough areas like East Texas and the
Hill Country and the Panhandle will be responsible,” Mr. O’Rourke said.
Mr. Henson added that while he remained skeptical about Democratic
enthusiasm being sufficient to carry the day for Mr. Talarico, he also
doubted that a last-minute avalanche of negative ads would prove decisive
for Mr. Paxton. “At a certain point, there’s diminishing impact once you
get past an absurd level of spending,” he said. Rather than project a
winner in November, Mr. Henson said he felt more comfortable embracing a
“gradualist” theory, one in which Texas does not become blue overnight,
but instead competitive. “Even if Talarico loses by a Beto-like margin,”
he said, “the next cycle is a presidential election, where Trump likely
won’t be popular and Democratic turnout will be higher. So there are
reasons for Texas Democrats to be optimistic.”'

According to a September survey conducted by Texas Southern University, Mr. Trump is seven points underwater in Texas. Mr. Talarico has run an energetic and well-financed campaign, while Mr. Paxton has staged far fewer public events and has had to rely on outside groups to fund an attack-ad blitzkrieg against his Democratic opponent. Mr. Abbott, meanwhile, has outspent Ms. Hinojosa by a 10-to-one ratio, yet has been unable to build an insurmountable lead. “People have vastly underestimated Gina,” said Ms. Davis, now a political consultant and a senior adviser to Planned Parenthood Texas Votes, an advocacy organization. “Dollar for dollar, she’s running the best statewide campaign we’ve ever seen.” Such optimism stands in defiance of the political axiom that Texas is where idealistic Democrats go to be mugged by reality. The party’s demise there is not a product of ill fortune, Mr. Henson said. “Governor Abbott has built an impressive election machine that has benefited state-level Republicans again and again for a decade and a half,” he said. “And the Democratic machinery here is almost nonexistent.” A ‘Hollowing-Out’ I have written about the politics of my native state at regular intervals for more than three decades. After watching the Democrats’ century-long rule in Texas come to a decisive end with Gov. Ann Richards’s loss to George W. Bush in 1994, I saw the party descend into atrophy in which failure begot more failure. “The 30-year drought has done a lot of things,” said Luke Warford, the chairman of the Travis County Democratic Party and the founder of the Agave Democratic Infrastructure Fund. “It’s kept donors on the sidelines, which makes a lot of potentially good candidates not run because there’s no belief they can win. And it also makes a lot of really talented staff leave to find better-paying work in true battleground states.” The Democratic Party has no counterpart to Mr. Abbott, and hasn’t since 1993, when Senator Lloyd Bentsen moved to Washington to join President Bill Clinton’s cabinet. Its weaknesses are even more glaring farther down the hierarchy. In recent elections, as many as one-third of state races have gone uncontested by Democrats. One-fifth of the party’s county chairs and two-thirds of its precinct chairs have been left unfilled. Until last year, the state party had a negative operating budget. As the veteran Democratic consultant Matt Angle observed, “There’s been a hollowing-out of the party.” Still, those of us who recall the satisfied sense of invincibility among Texas Democrats after roughly a century of one-party rule have detected similar signs of overconfidence among the state’s ruling party. The party’s rightward tilt, increasingly forceful with each legislative session, reached its apotheosis in March, with Mr. Paxton’s primary victory over the more moderate Republican four-term incumbent, Senator John Cornyn. Mr. Paxton, a close ally of Mr. Trump’s, was impeached by the Republican-controlled State House (and later acquitted by the State Senate) in 2023 over allegations that included bribery. He was also accused by his wife of adultery. Mr. Trump endorsed him anyway, all but guaranteeing his landslide primary triumph over Mr. Cornyn but in the process testing the allegiance of center-right Texans. In similar fashion, the Texas G.O.P. is in danger of losing many Latino voters who voted for Mr. Trump in 2024 after years of siding with Democrats. “We adopted a lazy way of campaigning that bit us on the ass, and we’ve learned from that,” Mr. O’Rourke said. “Now it’s the Republicans who’ve gotten really lazy and complacent and comfortable.” Signs of Republican Overreach Simply spending one week driving through the vastness of Texas, as I did in September, is all it takes to appreciate an underdog party’s uphill battle. The state’s 32 million residents are spread across 20 media markets, many of them distinct ecosystems, from the urban colossi of Houston and the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex to the oil patch of the Texas Panhandle to the Latino-dominated borderlands of the Rio Grande Valley. “When national donors are deciding where to invest, they look at a place like Iowa, where $5 million can fully fund a race,” said Katherine Fischer, the director of the Texas Majority PAC, which was established by the liberal philanthropist Soros family. “That’s why Texas is always at the bottom of their list. It’s just so damned big.” Reaching so many markets presents a daunting challenge for an upstart candidate like Ms. Hinojosa, a state representative from the border city of Brownsville. “There’s still 20 percent of the electorate that doesn’t know who I am,” she said in an interview in mid-September. To date, Ms. Hinojosa’s campaign has said that it has raised about $20 million. For his part, Mr. Talarico spent about $30 million earlier this year to introduce himself statewide as a man of Christian faith and a member of the Texas House with a record of supporting bipartisan legislation. Since that time, however, Mr. Paxton and his associates have invested more than $100 million in an effort to redefine his opponent as “radical” and “weird,” with ads that quote from remarks Mr. Talarico made several years ago (and later renounced) suggesting that “God is nonbinary” and that there are six biological sexes. Mr. Paxton and his allies have at times questioned Mr. Talarico’s manhood and even his Christianity, an effort to jolt the sensibilities of a state prone to mythologizing godly and masculine archetypes. “How they’re negatively defining Talarico is kind of a bank-shot way of saying that he’s not a true Texas conservative,” Mr. Henson said. Whether money can overwhelm conditions on the ground is the riddle looming over the Texas races. In the border city of Laredo, which Mr. Trump won in 2024 — the first time a Republican had done so in over a century — signs of buyer’s remorse are evident. Arrests by Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents in Laredo were higher in July than in any other American city. Mr. Trump’s erratic trade policies have further created instability at the city’s port of entry. While acknowledging the economic concerns that many border residents share, Adrian Zapata, a business executive in the health industry who voted for Mr. Trump in 2024, said in an interview that the negative ads against Mr. Talarico were resonating with some of his family members. “They see Talarico as an ultraliberal,” he said. “They’re done with the ‘they/them.’ They’re going to vote for Paxton just because of that.” As for Mr. Zapata, “I’m not ready to vote for Talarico,” he said. “But I don’t like Paxton. He’s never done anything for South Texas, and his personal and business dealings have hurt him a lot with folks down here.” There is a similarly muddled electoral picture in the cattle country of deep West Texas adjacent to Big Bend National Park. Mr. Trump and Mr. Abbott have aggressively championed a border wall and artificial intelligence data centers, both of which threaten to disrupt the region’s pastoral ethos. A coalition of more than 200 landowners has sued the federal government over the border wall, while other residents have circulated a petition to protest the construction of a new data center near Fort Stockton. George Johnson, a cattle feed operator in Alpine, waved off such concerns, saying: “Folks worrying about data centers were also worried when the internet got started. It’s Talarico who scares me to death, him and all that socialist talk.” Others in this largely conservative region harbor the view that Republicans have failed to make good on their promises. Thaddeus Cleveland, the Republican sheriff of Terrell County, said that both he and his county had voted for Mr. Trump in 2024, but added, “Everything he campaigned on, we’re seeing the opposite of, like going to war.” Sheriff Cleveland predicted that the negative campaign ads by the Republicans would not factor as significantly into the votes of his neighbors as “the price of groceries and gas, which are compounded here because we’re so far from everywhere else.” But it is in purple Tarrant County, dominated by Fort Worth, where the party could pay the price for having potentially overestimated its mandate from the voters. Conservative leaders have cut funds for nonprofits that aid at-risk children, subjected school library books to right-wing litmus tests and eliminated free bus rides to polling stations in poor neighborhoods. “The far-right leaders here have implemented Project 2025 on a county level,” said Alisa Simmons, a Democrat and county commissioner who is running to unseat the conservative county judge, Tim O’Hare. In an early sign this year that area Republicans may be out of step with Tarrant County’s constituents, a Democratic aviation machinist and union leader, Taylor Rehmet, defeated Leigh Wambsganss, a well-funded Republican Christian activist who led the conservative takeover of several metroplex school boards. He won by 14 points in a January special election for a State Senate seat covering a region that Mr. Trump won by 17 points in 2024. A ‘Gradualist’ Theory Which party prevails in Texas is a complicated riddle. Historically a low-turnout state — it ranked second to last in the 2024 election, ahead of only Arkansas — Texas held a primary in March that saw nearly one in four voters showing up to the polls, a modern record for midterm participation, with Democrats slightly outpacing Republicans. A few factors could conspire to thwart a blue wave in Texas. As of 2020, straight-ticket voting is no longer possible in the state, which could impact the mostly Democratic urban counties where that practice has frequently been used by voters in past elections. Texas is one of only eight states that lack universal online registration, while voting by mail is also highly restricted. In January, Mr. Abbott turned over the state’s list of approximately 18.7 million registered voters to the Trump administration, and 1.2 million of them have subsequently been put on the “suspense list” because their addresses have not been verified. The recent shuttering of nearly one-third of Tarrant County’s polling sites by its Republican-controlled county commission is particularly worrisome for Democrats. “The reason we’ve lost these statewide races in the past is because we’ve never gotten enough out of Tarrant County to overcome the margins in rural Texas,” Ms. Davis said of the turnout. “If we don’t get it to 53 or 54 percent this November, it’s game over. James and Gina can’t win.” But the state’s Republicans have reasons of their own to be fretful. Partly because of the recruitment efforts of the Texas Majority PAC and Blueprint Texas, a down-ballot candidate support organization co-founded by Ms. Davis earlier this year, the Democrats are fielding a full slate in all 150 state races for the first time in a half-century. Though many of these aspirants face long odds, their presence on the ballot could energize the Democrats in predominantly conservative regions who have not bothered to turn out in the past. “If we win on Nov. 3, most of those names running down-ballot in really tough areas like East Texas and the Hill Country and the Panhandle will be responsible,” Mr. O’Rourke said. Mr. Henson added that while he remained skeptical about Democratic enthusiasm being sufficient to carry the day for Mr. Talarico, he also doubted that a last-minute avalanche of negative ads would prove decisive for Mr. Paxton. “At a certain point, there’s diminishing impact once you get past an absurd level of spending,” he said. Rather than project a winner in November, Mr. Henson said he felt more comfortable embracing a “gradualist” theory, one in which Texas does not become blue overnight, but instead competitive. “Even if Talarico loses by a Beto-like margin,” he said, “the next cycle is a presidential election, where Trump likely won’t be popular and Democratic turnout will be higher. So there are reasons for Texas Democrats to be optimistic.”' You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:

subject: I’m actually concerned
disclaimer_text: Paid for by VPP
body:
| [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/141517?t=6&akid=30696%2E878179%2EvKVaNs) I’m concerned, but not in the B.S. way Susan was “concerned” on the debate stage for all four debates.

I’m actually concerned, because despite four debates that showed just how corrupt and out of touch Susan Collins is, we’re still falling behind on our midnight goal. And we have just hours to reach it. [Will you chip in now to ensure the Voter Protection Project and I have the cash to defeat Susan Collins in 9 days?](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/141517?t=7&akid=30696%2E878179%2EvKVaNs) | [CHIP IN NOW →](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/141517?t=8&akid=30696%2E878179%2EvKVaNs)
---
During all four debates, Susan was “concerned” and “frustrated” when her bad votes, connections to Trump, and complete abandonment of Mainers were brought up.

**She can’t handle being held accountable for the consequences of her actions.**

The part that gets me the most is that Susan could actually do something about it if she wanted to.

Susan Collins has voted with Donald Trump 96% of the time, then claims to be bipartisan. It’s no surprise considering that her corporate PACs and billionaire buddies have spent $60 million to defeat me.

**In the Senate, I’ll do things differently.**

This seat and your vote can only be earned, not bought. I don’t take any corporate PAC money, and I sure as hell don’t take your support for granted.

I’ve known since day one that if we were going to win this race, it had to be from the bottom up, grassroots-powered through and through. And so far, we’ve made it work. We are catching up to Susan on the airwaves and in the polls.

**But tonight, we’re at risk of falling short of our $1,000,000 midnight goal.**

If we fall short, Susan will dominate the airwaves, and we will slip in the polls. With just 9 days until the Election, we have no time to take a step back.

[This is our one shot to flip this seat and the Senate, so we can’t fall short. So, as much as I hate asking for money, will you chip in before midnight to help the Voter Protection Project and me retire Susan Collins and her infinite “concern” once and for all? → ](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/141517?t=9&akid=30696%2E878179%2EvKVaNs)
[CHIP IN NOW →](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/141517?t=10&akid=30696%2E878179%2EvKVaNs)

Solidarity forever,
Troy Jackson

Every abuse of these past two years traces back to extremist politicians who no longer need their voters’ approval to keep their seats.
Rig the map, and you never have to answer for anything again.
That is why one of my first bills will be the Let Voters Choose Act, a national ban on partisan gerrymandering.
Maps drawn by independent commissions after each census, and no more carving up cities and counties that belong together.
James Talarico has pledged to fight for the same reform from the Senate.

They walked out carrying boxes of evidence. | Friends, Federal agents raided adult day care centers in Brooklyn, Queens and Staten Island on Tuesday. They walked out carrying boxes of evidence. The suspected crimes: money laundering, kickbacks and billing Medicaid for care that may never have been provided. | | This is not a small leak. New York’s Medicaid program paid roughly $2.4 billion for social adult day care between 2019 and 2024. Those costs ran 40 to 60 percent above the national average. More than 100 providers are now under investigation. That is your money. It was supposed to care for New York’s seniors. | Here is the question nobody in Albany wants to answer. Where was New York’s independent watchdog? Democrat Tom DiNapoli has sat in the Comptroller’s chair for nearly 20 years. A program ran 40 to 60 percent hotter than the rest of the country, year after year, and New Yorkers found out from an FBI raid. That is what reactive oversight looks like. The waste gets discovered after the money is already gone. Every dollar New Yorkers send to Albany was earned by someone working hard for it. It deserves to be guarded like it matters. | Here is what I will do: Flag high-risk Medicaid payments in real time, before the checks clear. Audit providers whose costs are wildly out of line with the rest of the country. Publish what we find, so taxpayers see it** before the FBI has to. Hi, are you paying attention to what's happening in Maine right now?
My friend, Troy Jackson, is in a neck-and-neck race against Susan Collins. He's being outspent by the millions, and needs our help to win this fight.
**[Forecasters are predicting Troy's race will determine control of the Senate. The stakes couldn't be higher. If you care about winning Maine, please give $10 to support Troy right now.](https://substack.com/redirect/d1f22d28-780d-43a1-87ff-d34b01e4b439?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[DONATE TO TROY JACKSON'S CAMPAIGN ->](https://substack.com/redirect/d1f22d28-780d-43a1-87ff-d34b01e4b439?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Listen, here's how we got here:
First, Democrats across the country warned that Maine would be one of the closest Senate races in the country.
Then, Susan Collins and Donald Trump got scared. They're going to spend $114 million to drown Troy Jackson out on television and on the ground.
**Now, a recent New York Times poll came out that shows Troy losing ground to Susan - 46% to 49%.**
This is the worst possible time to be losing ground, so Troy needs our help TODAY. Not tomorrow, not one week from now.
Don't forget: We need to win Maine to give ourselves the best possible shot at retaking the Senate.
**[This is one of the most important races to get involved in before the election, but we need to act fast. Please, give $10- or more if you can swing it - before midnight to help elect Troy Jackson and take back the Senate.](https://substack.com/redirect/d1f22d28-780d-43a1-87ff-d34b01e4b439?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

I appreciate you acting fast.
\- Gavin Newsom

body:
Hello everyone!

My name is Brandon, I'm a Deputy Organizing Director with the Michigan One Team Coordinated Campaign! I'm reaching out on behalf of Jenny with Ben Ambrose's team, who is running for Congress in Michigan's 2nd congressional district.

We have just eight days left until Election Day, and I am happy to share our canvassing opportunities across the 2nd congressional district over the final four days of the campaign, beginning on Saturday, October 31.

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: I want to take a moment to talk about faith
body:
Taking a leap of faith.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
In just a minute, I’m going to personally ask you to **[make a donation to my campaign for governor.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261025_3_faith.pw32zy&refcode=em20261025-2527&t=1&akid=2527%2E299639%2EredY4V)**
Before I do, I hope you’ll let me share **an important lesson I’ve learned about faith.**
Back in 2021, the Texas GOP was ramming an extreme anti-voter bill through the State House. The voter suppression bill they were pushing was ugly. It was dangerous. And I knew that staying put would mean letting Texans lose their freedom to vote.
So I took a leap of faith. I walked off the floor.
But I knew I couldn’t stop this bill on my own. I needed my fellow Democratic legislators with me in order to break quorum. So I stood up, and I texted other legislators:
_“A leap of faith only works if you take it.”_
Together, we ran out the clock and stopped a bill designed to silence Texas voters. That quorum break protected Sunday morning voting — a sacred tradition in Black churches — and blocked a provision that would have allowed partisan judges to overturn election results without evidence. And we earned that victory together.
**Just like I needed my fellow Texas Democrats by my side on that day five years ago, I’m asking you to join me today.** I’m asking you to have faith that we can finally unseat corrupt Governor Greg Abbott and flip Texas together.
Each time you chip in to our people-powered campaign, you’re doing it alongside thousands of others who also believe in our power to win a brighter future for every Texan.
**[Can I count on you to donate to my grassroots campaign and help me defeat Greg Abbott on November 3rd?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261025_3_faith.pw32zy&refcode=em20261025-2527&t=2&akid=2527%2E299639%2EredY4V)**

_A leap of faith only works if you take it._ And when you do, others will leap with you.
— Gina

We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=3736%2E259176%2EI3sDhN) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=3736%2E259176%2EI3sDhN)_

We're just over a week out from Election Day, and the pressure is on. But not for the reasons you might think...

The truth is: **I don’t want to let you down.**

_You_ are the heart of this campaign. Since the very beginning, grassroots donors have made it possible to compete with massive spending from special interests. You’ve proven that when working people come together, we can win:
* When Peter Thiel dropped $3.6 million against me in a single week, you helped keep our own ads live.
* When JD Vance personally attacked me, you stood by me and helped this campaign surge ahead.
* And when crypto billionaires decided to put $30 million behind new attack ads spreading lies about me, you helped us fight back.

But this race is far from over, Peter.

All eyes are on Ohio, and the money continues to _pour_ in. In fact, Republican megadonors are spending more here than in Georgia, Alaska, and North Carolina combined. Let that sink in.

I’m not sharing this to scare you – the polls keep proving that we have what it takes to win – but I’m writing this to remind you just how important you are to this movement.

**In the face of a quarter of a BILLION dollars being spent by Republicans in Ohio, our campaign has been able to stay competitive _only_ because of grassroots donations from folks like you. And right now, I need you to have my back more than ever.**

My past races have taught me that this close to Election Day, resources are what allow a candidate to pull ahead. So we cannot give the GOP an inch. You may have seen what’s going on in the Ohio governor’s race, between Vivek Ramaswamy and Amy Acton.
#

Friend,
I’ve been doing this job for a little while now, and I’ve gotten a pretty good sense of what can happen when you decide to get into politics.
You get lies told about you in the media, in television ads. People you’ve never met drag your name through the mud. It can get out of hand fast, and I’ve seen quite a bit. But even I can still be shocked.
You may have seen what’s going on in the Ohio governor’s race, between Vivek Ramaswamy and Amy Acton. Many others have already covered this so I won’t get into all that much detail. But Vivek is running attack ads featuring Amy’s mother, who Amy has been estranged from for decades after serious abuse she suffered as a child. He’s refused to take it down.
The campaign ad is one thing, and it’s the lowest form of politics. But what’s worse is that, given the opportunity to rebuke this stuff, National Republicans are actually backing Vivek and the ad — all the way up to Trump and Vance.
This is the kind of politics we have come to expect from the people “leading” this country. This is what they offer us. But friend, it doesn’t have to be this way. And to me, the best thing we can do to show that is to back Amy with everything we’ve got.
[**I’m asking you to split a donation between Amy’s campaign for governor and mine. ************************___**Photos and Video[**HERE**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.yjJN_MEbNx94PLaWzZ6hW1GJm7fH52LAiTq9C8yR9M8whqGpOOSRmcHe-1Wx9m9NAlVUYMyGFzUVnGKnLIyQCqkhosDxpfvsE1OJb4N9zwluITt3DyRp1PZTQEGVJ-h-B5oHjGbITSxDd-l567FVC09-WrzEfaZJXCspme1SlmtE4N7wXH2gOCd2T7JKgbjY8RRg9iKfdkLBxJgP9COkU9nIAQ-0urApVpx_PtCJ1cWsb5sH3pxO0-ELiuslhQ0tnIQxNv8avAqhmyOZ2_LGQCcKTEPET00BRZEGIasH9wucYxx3EO90NY4-U9nm67WOIHoy_do55KHkCw2pXPItTuhc0HRiLsbZBupgwz8ckqlBSwn0wgD23UehnlSnqXHldMmJ_z1oMMjiXsz56JhW2kjldrRMmjkEKVLpUqVOXGhsjWSfE0GkZmSmYYqizYFYGmGXBQNFZMq9WGvMSLzM7aFOh4DC0CkWqcHvytFjZ2146KSid05eK_uzL6Xkna7Q/4v6/UcE4xNDFR1WeudAlPEJRDw/h0/h001.3jsx3DGWtJ89qvUM5xMuxvsYlVekWsMzmJGCBacjCbA)**___
__**************PEEKSKILL, NY –** Cait Conley, Army combat veteran and Democratic nominee for New York’s 17th Congressional District, was joined yesterday in Peekskill by House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, Speaker Adrienne Adams, local elected officials, and hundreds of union organizers and community members for a rally to kick off Early Voting. “Clear choices in front of all of the people of the Hudson Valley and Westchester and beyond in terms of the stakes of this election. On the one hand, we can continue to have a Republican-controlled Congress that's been a disaster for the American people. And on the other hand, we can take back control of the House and dramatically change direction in the United States of America. **" It's all about Americans coming together, doing what's right for the country...The Republicans have had their chance in the state of Kentucky, and things aren't getting better. So it's time for a change."**
That's what my new friend, Nathan White, had to say when asked why he is supporting my campaign.
I met him on the campaign trail recently, and his message resembled what a lot of Kentuckians I've met have had to say.
They're done voting for politicians who push them to the sidelines because they're too busy trying to get rich - just like Mitch McConnell and his chosen heir, Andy Barr.
As long as corporate PACS and billionaires are lining their pockets, special interests will always come before yours. Andy has already become a millionaire since taking office in the House - have you gotten any richer?
I'm running to deliver the leadership that Kentuckians are long overdue for.
And in this home stretch, I'm pulling out all the stops to bring this grassroots movement to Washington and end the cycle of special interests coming before working families.
Mail-in ballots are already being sent in. Early Voting is in 4 days. My opponent and I are tied. Will you chip in to my Senate campaign today?

| | | |
---
| | | Patriot,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

Patriot, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story...

It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now.

So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together.

Young people face that pressure every single day.

They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is.

JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion.

He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back.

That's what _Communion_ is about...

And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now.

That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith.

Friend 🐾,

I’m barking in your inbox today because I’ve been one busy pup! My mom brought me along to a very special place: **Chaco Canyon!**
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17387?refcode=jtk1661-fr-nd&t=2&akid=13400%2E400544%2E1CGyRH)
I got to explore, take in all the new smells, and spend some time outside with my mom. But I know Chaco isn’t just a great place for a walk. It’s a sacred place that means so much to my mom, Tribal communities, and generations of New Mexicans.
**Chaco holds a special place in my mom’s heart. She’s spent years fighting to protect it and the other sacred lands that make New Mexico so special. And as Governor, she’ll keep fighting to make sure these places are here for generations to come._But she can’t do it alone_. ****[Will you paw-lease chip in $5 or $10 today to give my mom the resources she needs to win this election and keep protecting New Mexico?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17387?refcode=jtk1661-fr-nd&t=3&akid=13400%2E400544%2E1CGyRH)**

I may be just a pup, but even I know there’s something special about this place. I watched my mom take it all in, and I could tell Chaco means more to her than just a beautiful place to visit.
It reminded her of all the time she spent outside with her dad. She grew up running through the desert with her cousins and fishing with him. Those memories taught her that we have a responsibility to take care of the places we call home.

_And that’s why she’s so worried about what’s happening right now._
Donald Trump is moving to slash protections for the lands surrounding Chaco and reopen them to mining and oil and gas drilling. **That means putting a place that has been sacred to Indigenous peoples since time immemorial at risk.**

**My mom says Chaco is not for sale.**

Team Abdul

Normally when you see my name in your inbox, I like the messages to be different from the other emails you get from most elected officials.
I've written to you in detail about the depth of corruption and self-enrichment of the Trump Administration, the President's thirst for political retribution and intimidation, along with other things I am seeing or working on in Washington, D.C. and at home in Georgia.
This message is different. It's more direct.
I am reaching out today with a humble request for a contribution to my campaign. Here's why:
Voting is underway in Georgia, and we have to treat every day like Election Day. We have to work relentlessly to turn out the voters we need to decisively win this race.
_**Because Georgia remains the pivotal battleground state.**_
I won this Senate seat by just 1.2% in 2021, and Republicans are determined to defeat me and take it back. That's why JD Vance and Donald Trump both came to Georgia this month to rally their supporters and uplift my opponent, Mike Collins.
There are many paths to a Democratic Senate majority. **But all of those paths depend upon defending this seat in Georgia.**
So with less than 9 days until the polls close, it's time to take action and use the power that we have as citizens to make a difference and regain Congressional power.
**[We have to win, and we have to win decisively on November 3. So I 'm asking, humbly, if you will chip in to my reelection campaign today.](https://substack.com/redirect/b17625ad-d7b8-4661-af49-76835ed08259?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[CONTRIBUTE](https://substack.com/redirect/b17625ad-d7b8-4661-af49-76835ed08259?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Let's not wonder what more we might have done after the polls close.
Thank you,
Jon

We have more people that agree with our vision for TX-09 (cut taxes, invest in key infrastructure, unleash the oil & gas industry, support our Ag industry and keep the border secure) but if our people stay home – a corrupt lobbyist who built a career attacking industry and our jobs will end up in this seat.**Next Steps:****(1)** Download the [Abbott Impact App](https://us.list-manage.com/KCa7VaDJNHb?e=2f22037b53&c2id=7754ab9baad365fc79c8a2e86cd53f4b), a free app that allows you to see which of your friends and family (from your contacts) haven’t voted yet so you can send them reminders to go vote**(2)** Go vote and bring your friends - **Texas and the next generation are worth protecting!**

My name is Adam Kinzinger. You might know me as one of the only Republicans who served on the January 6th Committee, and one of 10 Republicans who voted to impeach Donald Trump.
I’ll be straight with you — I served in the House as a Republican for 12 years. But I’m doing what I can to help re-elect Eugene Vindman to Congress. Because at the end of the day, our democracy matters more than party or politics. And I have immense respect for people who believe in something, and hold fast to it regardless of pressure. Eugene is the textbook example of service and patriotism.
Like me, Eugene is a veteran.
I served this country flying KC-135s and RC-26Bs with multiple tours in Iraq and Afghanistan, and Eugene is a retired U.S. Army officer who served our nation with distinction, including on the National Security Council, where he stood up for what was right when the stakes couldn’t be higher.
We both took an oath to the Constitution — and we’ve both lived that oath through service and sacrifice.
Eugene and I won’t agree on everything. But I trust him to tell the truth, continue to fight for our democracy, and put the country ahead of politics.
But it’s going to take all of us doing our part to make sure leaders like Eugene can continue to serve.

clean_body: Friend, My name is Emily, and I'm a ballot chaser for Turning Point PAC in Arizona. That means every day, I show up, knock on doors, have conversations with potential voters, and chase down ballots before Election Day. I need to tell you what I'm seeing out here, because I don't think most people understand how close this really is. Arizona is not lost.Not even close. But it is not safe either. A new poll just showed Katie Hobbs up by 4 points over Andy Biggs. Four points. That is the entire ballgame, sitting right there behind the doors I have not knocked on yet. Turning Point PAC is not like anything else in this space. They take decades of grassroots organizing and put real people, like me, into these communities well before Election Day. We build relationships. We knock on the same doors more than once. We chase every ballot, mail-in or in person, because every single one counts. This is the vision Charlie Kirk built. People on the ground, having real conversations, changing real minds. And it is working! But I cannot do this alone, and neither can the 700 of us out here across Arizona. I 'm seeing momentum on the ground, but we have so many more voters to cover. We can't do it without your continued support. Every $50 you give sponsors a ballot chaser like me for one full day. That's about 75 doors and 25 real conversations with voters who haven't made up their minds yet, and who deserve to hear from us before it's too late. | | Friend, For Minnesota’s miners, farmers, construction workers, and other working families, retirement is something you earn after a lifetime on the job.**Social Security helps make sure that hard work pays off. ** In the rural parts of our state, where many workers have limited access to employer-sponsored retirement plans or pensions, Social Security is especially important. It helps retirees afford groceries, heating bills, housing, and prescriptions.
---

body:
October 25, 2026 | Read Online ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/4zu3km9d6vtehpoo67dcxh66p4x0rh5h4g0zl/qvh8h7hd3dg0l9ilhk/aHR0cHM6Ly9ja2FyY2hpdmUuY29tL2IvMHZ1d2g5aDk4OGdwNmY3bWdncm16aHZ2MG0zbmRjbmg4NXFtZA== )

From Catherine
--------------

Support True the Vote’s work ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/4zu3km9d6vtehpoo67dcxh66p4x0rh5h4g0zl/3ohphkh3836nk8trhn/aHR0cHM6Ly90cnVldGhldm90ZS5vcmcvZG9uYXRl )

Hi Friend —

Keeping up with the news these days means constantly sorting through what’s true, what’s distorted, and what’s been made up entirely ... it’s exhausting, but necessary.

This week, we learned that fabricated polls have defined this season's national election coverage — the very numbers relied upon to tell the country who’s winning were bogus.

In election season, polling can build or break momentum. Polls drive headlines, influence donations, and shape whether people believe their vote will matter.

That’s why this week’s revelation was so consequential. Wedgewood Polls, a provider of 15 polls included in the New York Times’ polling tracker, admitted that all but one of its polls had been fabricated. Invented numbers were presented as the voice of the American people, with the credibility of the Times behind them.

( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/4zu3km9d6vtehpoo67dcxh66p4x0rh5h4g0zl/8ghqhoho8oex8pukh9/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubnl0aW1lcy5jb20vMjAyNi8xMC8yMS91cy9taWR0ZXJtLWVsZWN0aW9uLWZha2UtcG9sbGluZy13ZWRnZXdvb2QuaHRtbA== )
Even legitimate polling faces challenges in today's culture. Pew’s telephone response rate fell from 36% in 1997 to 6% in 2018, and researchers find growing evidence that Republicans are less likely than Democrats to participate.

The industry’s own review found that late polls overstated Democratic margins by 3.1 points in 2016, 4.6 in 2020, and 2.7 in 2024. Recent midterm polls performed better, but the record calls for humility. Instead, uncertain numbers become confident declarations about who’s winning and who should give up.

For those of us who cherish liberty, pessimism can begin to feel like realism. We value honesty. We keep our word. We expect fair dealing. Watching those standards violated again and again wears on us. Our confidence suffers, and eventually, expecting the worst can feel like the only sensible position.

But that is a conclusion we need to examine, too.

The dishonesty is real, but it does not mean that goodness is scarce, that we stand alone, or that our efforts are futile. A steady diet of betrayal and dysfunction has distorted understandings of our country and of one another.

We must bring discernment to everything. Don't be too quick to believe the hype. What supports it? What does it leave out? Have we mistaken what dominates the headlines for what defines the country?

Talk to your neighbors. Spend time in your community. A conversation across the kitchen table is real. So are the good people quietly keeping their promises, helping others, and doing their part. We have a part in strengthening that goodness, too.

And voting is real. The process is imperfect and protecting it takes work — your participation is critical.

We’ve added a way to check your early voting activity through Scan. Check. Protect., including whether your ballot has been recorded in the data the states release. Updates follow state reporting schedules; recorded activity does not confirm inclusion in the final count.

( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/4zu3km9d6vtehpoo67dcxh66p4x0rh5h4g0zl/7qh7h8h9e9vmewazh6/aHR0cHM6Ly9zY2FuY2hlY2twcm90ZWN0Lm9yZw== )
Visit ScanCheckProtect.org ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/4zu3km9d6vtehpoo67dcxh66p4x0rh5h4g0zl/7qh7h8h9e9vmewazh6/aHR0cHM6Ly9zY2FuY2hlY2twcm90ZWN0Lm9yZw== ), check your record, check activity at your address, and encourage someone else to do the same.

Last week, I wrote about answering the call: “Here am I. Send me. ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/4zu3km9d6vtehpoo67dcxh66p4x0rh5h4g0zl/p8heh9h4e4klerhqh3/aHR0cHM6Ly9uZXdzbGV0dGVyLnRydWV0aGV2b3RlLm9yZy9wb3N0cy9oZXJlLWFtLWktc2VuZC1tZS1hLWJpcnRoZGF5LWxlc3Nvbg== )” That call still stands. Learning something difficult, like fraud in polling, changes our understanding of what we face. It doesn’t diminish our ability — or our responsibility — to take a stand and make a difference.

God has given us minds to reason, neighbors to love, work to do, and infinite reasons to keep hope alive.

Never quit. Ephesians 6 and Isaiah 6:8 FTW!

Ever onward —

( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/4zu3km9d6vtehpoo67dcxh66p4x0rh5h4g0zl/58hvh7hgwgpzw8h6h4/aHR0cHM6Ly9wZW9wbGVzcG9sbC5jb20= )
P.S. Looking for a clearer read on the polls? Our friends at Onward Media built People's Poll, a fresh take on polling. It tracks every published 2026 Senate, governor and House poll and links each one to its source, so you can check the numbers yourself. Take a look at peoplespoll.com ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/4zu3km9d6vtehpoo67dcxh66p4x0rh5h4g0zl/58hvh7hgwgpzw8h6h4/aHR0cHM6Ly9wZW9wbGVzcG9sbC5jb20= ).

A message from someone you know moves people to vote in a way mass campaign messages can't.

* Texts from friends boost turnout. In a Columbia University study, a text from a friend raised turnout 8.3 percentage points. Mass automated texts average less than half a point.
* Small margins decide big elections. Just 187 votes decided a seat in Congress in 2024. Reaching even a few friends makes a real difference.
* Connection and a plan. What works is a friendly nudge from someone you trust, plus help making a real plan: when, where and how you'll vote.

Simple ways to help your seven: share their polling place, send date reminders, or offer a ride or a hand.

North Carolina: One Voter. Multiple Records?
--------------------------------------------

A new complaint alleges 3,674 sets of duplicate or triplicate voter registrations in North Carolina. The state acknowledges ongoing cleanup efforts, but the watchdog group wants systemic fixes. Because cleaning voter rolls shouldn't be a never-ending game of whack-a-mole.

Don't forget! You can check your own voter registration record and your activity right now. Visit scancheckprotect.org ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/4zu3km9d6vtehpoo67dcxh66p4x0rh5h4g0zl/7qh7h8h9e9vmewazh6/aHR0cHM6Ly9zY2FuY2hlY2twcm90ZWN0Lm9yZw== ) and take three minutes to:

* Confirm your current record is accurate — your name, address, and status.
* See if your early vote was recorded — check back if your state hasn't reported yet.
* Verify that your address isn't being used as a voter trap house — after you pull up your record, check your current address and confirm you recognize anyone else who may be registered at your residence.
* Check the rolls in states where you used to live — old registrations often linger for years after you've moved, sometimes without your knowledge.
* Tell us what you found. Good or bad, we want to hear from you — and if something looks off, we're here to help you fix it.

clean_body: October 25, 2026 | Read Online ( == ) From Catherine Support True the Vote’s work ( ) Hi Friend — Keeping up with the news these days means constantly sorting through what’s true, what’s distorted, and what’s been made up entirely ... it’s exhausting, but necessary. This week, we learned that fabricated polls have defined this season's national election coverage — the very numbers relied upon to tell the country who’s winning were bogus. In election season, polling can build or break momentum. Polls drive headlines, influence donations, and shape whether people believe their vote will matter. That’s why this week’s revelation was so consequential. Wedgewood Polls, a provider of 15 polls included in the New York Times’ polling tracker, admitted that all but one of its polls had been fabricated. Invented numbers were presented as the voice of the American people, with the credibility of the Times behind them. ( == ) Even legitimate polling faces challenges in today's culture. Pew’s telephone response rate fell from 36% in 1997 to 6% in 2018, and researchers find growing evidence that Republicans are less likely than Democrats to participate. The industry’s own review found that late polls overstated Democratic margins by 3.1 points in 2016, 4.6 in 2020, and 2.7 in 2024. Recent midterm polls performed better, but the record calls for humility. Instead, uncertain numbers become confident declarations about who’s winning and who should give up. For those of us who cherish liberty, pessimism can begin to feel like realism. We value honesty. We keep our word. We expect fair dealing. Watching those standards violated again and again wears on us. Our confidence suffers, and eventually, expecting the worst can feel like the only sensible position. But that is a conclusion we need to examine, too. The dishonesty is real, but it does not mean that goodness is scarce, that we stand alone, or that our efforts are futile. A steady diet of betrayal and dysfunction has distorted understandings of our country and of one another. We must bring discernment to everything. Don't be too quick to believe the hype. What supports it? What does it leave out? Have we mistaken what dominates the headlines for what defines the country? Talk to your neighbors. Spend time in your community. A conversation across the kitchen table is real. So are the good people quietly keeping their promises, helping others, and doing their part. We have a part in strengthening that goodness, too. And voting is real. The process is imperfect and protecting it takes work — your participation is critical. We’ve added a way to check your early voting activity through Scan. Check. Protect., including whether your ballot has been recorded in the data the states release. Updates follow state reporting schedules; recorded activity does not confirm inclusion in the final count. ( == ) Visit ScanCheckProtect.org ( == ), check your record, check activity at your address, and encourage someone else to do the same. Last week, I wrote about answering the call: “Here am I. Send me. ( == )” That call still stands. Learning something difficult, like fraud in polling, changes our understanding of what we face. It doesn’t diminish our ability — or our responsibility — to take a stand and make a difference. God has given us minds to reason, neighbors to love, work to do, and infinite reasons to keep hope alive. Never quit. Ephesians 6 and Isaiah 6:8 FTW! Ever onward — ( = ) P.S. Looking for a clearer read on the polls? Our friends at Onward Media built People's Poll, a fresh take on polling. It tracks every published 2026 Senate, governor and House poll and links each one to its source, so you can check the numbers yourself. Take a look at peoplespoll.com ( = ). Help us keep going Your gift helps True the Vote keep tools like Scan. Check. Protect. available to voters. -->Give today ( ) Give today ( ) ( ) A message from someone you know moves people to vote in a way mass campaign messages can't. Texts from friends boost turnout. In a Columbia University study, a text from a friend raised turnout 8.3 percentage points. Mass automated texts average less than half a point. Small margins decide big elections. Just 187 votes decided a seat in Congress in 2024. Reaching even a few friends makes a real difference. Connection and a plan. What works is a friendly nudge from someone you trust, plus help making a real plan: when, where and how you'll vote. Simple ways to help your seven: share their polling place, send date reminders, or offer a ride or a hand. -->Get started at 7votes.org ( ) Get started at 7votes.org ( ) Sources: Schein, Green et al., Columbia University, friend-to-friend texting in the 2018 midterms; 2024 U.S. House results. In other news ... ( ) Placeholder Votes..? Questions are mounting over alleged discrepancies between early-voting check-ins and voter history records in Georgia. Could missing records indicate processing errors, or something more serious? Without timely, verifiable check-in records, the public is left asking questions. Election transparency shouldn't require guesswork. Read the Post ( ) ( ) North Carolina: One Voter. Multiple Records? A new complaint alleges 3,674 sets of duplicate or triplicate voter registrations in North Carolina. The state acknowledges ongoing cleanup efforts, but the watchdog group wants systemic fixes. Because cleaning voter rolls shouldn't be a never-ending game of whack-a-mole. Read More ( ) ( == ) Don't forget! You can check your own voter registration record and your activity right now. Visit scancheckprotect.org ( == ) and take three minutes to: Confirm your current record is accurate — your name, address, and status. See if your early vote was recorded — check back if your state hasn't reported yet. Verify that your address isn't being used as a voter trap house — after you pull up your record, check your current address and confirm you recognize anyone else who may be registered at your residence. Check the rolls in states where you used to live — old registrations often linger for years after you've moved, sometimes without your knowledge. Tell us what you found.
